killed.claim: '--ease-standard… is an accelerate-then-decelerate curve designed for one-shot A→B transitions. Applied between the two stops of a symmetric loop it produces an asymmetric tick (slow-out on the way down, snap on the way back), not a breath.' (challenge-D-design.md:422-426)
killed.refutation: REFUTED twice over. (1) CSS Animations Level 1: animation-timing-function applies to EACH keyframe interval independently, not to the animation as a whole. offline-dot-pulse has stops at 0%, 50%, 100% (ApiOfflineChip.vue:82-85), so the identical curve governs the 0→50 leg and the 50→100 leg — the loop is symmetric by construction and no asymmetric tick can arise. (2) The curve is symmetric in kind: --ease-standard → --motion-ease-standard: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) (dist/styles/tokens/scheme-spring.css) is Material 'standard', an ease-IN-OUT, not an ease-in. The chosen token is the right shape for a breath.

killed.claim: 'chip fill (86,57,50) card well bg (86,57,50) → CR fill/well = 1.00… In dark mode the pill's background is pixel-identical to the card behind it. The 12%-destructive wash composites to nothing. There is no chip.' (challenge-D-design.md:90-100, 351)
killed.refutation: ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE given the CSS, for any ground. ApiOfflineChip.vue:71 composites color-mix(in oklab, var(--destructive) 12%, transparent) — a 12%-alpha ink — over ground G, giving 0.12·ink + 0.88·G, which equals G if and only if ink == G. Dark --destructive = hsl(0 80% 60%) = (235,71,71) (dist/styles/tokens/dark-arm.css) and D's own sampled ground is (86,57,50): the composite must be ≈(104,59,53), an 18-unit red lift, not identity. D's own dark ink sample (brightest pixel 235,71,71) confirms the token resolved, which makes the coincident fill/well samples self-contradictory. Most likely cause is the caveat D itself recorded at :54-56 — the classList.add('dark') hack did not re-derive the ground. The dark limb does not survive; the light limb does (see confirmed).

killed.claim: '3.58:1 is the honest read of the perceived stroke body' for the offline chip's text; D-15 lists 'the lowest text contrast (3.58:1 offline)'. (challenge-D-design.md:104-117, 489-493)
killed.refutation: The offline register PASSES AA. ApiOfflineChip.vue:52 color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground) 72%, transparent) over the chip's own fill computes to (88,85,82) on (243,239,234) — and D's own 'darkest pixel (88,85,82) → 6.47:1' is an exact match for that computation, i.e. D measured the correct value and then discarded it. The 3.58 figure is the mean of the darkest 2.5% of ANTIALIASED pixels; WCAG 1.4.3 is evaluated against the specified foreground and background colours, not subpixel coverage deciles. Using the antialiasing decile manufactures a sub-AA number for a register that is 6.47:1. The real cause of the washout is a different defect — see my missed finding on synthesized small caps.

missed.claim: font-variant: small-caps is BROWSER-SYNTHESIZED in every code path — the shipped Fira Code webfont has no small-caps table. This, not ink opacity, is the actual mechanism behind the 'partial coverage on almost every glyph pixel' the design seat observed and mis-attributed to contrast.
missed.proof: ApiOfflineChip.vue:44 font-variant: small-caps (and DockStatusLamp.vue:52) resolve through .fira-code (demo/styles/utils.css:9-11) → --font-mono: var(--font-stack-mono) → '"Fira Code", "Fira Code Fallback", "Fira Mono", monospace'. The actual face glass-ui ships is node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/fonts/fira-code/fira-code-latin.woff2; read with fontTools its GSUB feature list is exactly ['calt','dnom','frac','locl','numr'] — no smcp, no c2sc. Browsers therefore synthesize small caps by scaling capitals, thinning stems to sub-pixel weight at 11px with 0.06em tracking. The component picked the one spelling the shipped font cannot honour. Present in both twins, so it is also a glass-ui BH/BI relay item.

Whether .dashed-well's rendered dark-mode ground matches its token computation. My refutation of D-8's dark limb rests on the compositing identity (0.12·ink + 0.88·G = G iff ink = G), which holds for any G and needs no live read; the specific dark RGB values I derived are not independently observed.

No r2 file exists for any axis in this component directory (only challenge-C/D/L r1 plus evidence/), so AXIS-PROMOTIONS does not apply here; all three are EXISTS-ORIGINAL per registry/HYDRATION-LEDGER.md:42-44, i.e. self-authored seats, not the thin Codex batch.
superlatives: The reduced-motion idiom is the best thing in the file and better than the app's own default. ApiOfflineChip.vue:81-90 puts BOTH the @keyframes body and the animation declaration inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), so under reduce no animation exists to override — strictly stronger than the blunt global guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184-192 (animation-duration: 0.01ms !important on *), which still runs a 0.01ms animation and still fights the cascade. All three axes credited this (challenge-C-implementation.md:400-406, challenge-D-design.md:433-435, challenge-L-library.md:359-361) and all three are right.

The animated property is opacity and nothing else (ApiOfflineChip.vue:83-84) — compositor-only, no layout, no paint — and there is no rAF, timer, listener or observer anywhere in the SFC. No cleanup surface, therefore no unmount race and no leak class. In a repo whose own constellation audit recorded a ~40-site PRM-RAF epidemic, this leaf is clean by construction.

The misconfigured ≠ unavailable distinction at the latch is genuine engineering, not ceremony. availability.ts:20-35 states the CORS-vs-network indistinguishability problem honestly, :112-116 detects the precondition up front rather than mislabelling a symptom, :167-169 refuses to relabel the designed state, and :188-191 fails loud and synchronously. The component's only sin is giving that distinction two visible surfaces where it needed at most one.

The DI seam is exemplary and should survive every cure unchanged. ApiOfflineChip.vue:31,35 reads the latch through useApiClient() rather than importing the module singleton, exactly as useApiClient.ts:2-17 intends, with a correct fail-fast when no provider stands above (:54-61). L's negative proof calls it 'the one structural decision in the file that is right' (challenge-L-library.md:404-406) and that is the correct read.

Self-gating with no empty shell: unknown and available render nothing at all (ApiOfflineChip.vue:12,20) — no zero-height node, no skeleton, no placeholder reserving space in the well. The absence is the design.

The copy tells the truth, and the truth was engineered to be tellable. 'saved locally' is backed by usePaletteActions.ts:65-77, where onCurrentPaletteSaved runs createPalette UNCONDITIONALLY, with a comment recording that the prior `await ensureUser()` inverted the contract and silently destroyed palettes on an unreachable backend. A status string that would have been a lie six waves ago is now a fact. No axis checked this; it is the strongest thing in the component's cone.

One line consumes a token correctly and gets a free accessibility win for it: border: 1px solid var(--card-edge) (ApiOfflineChip.vue:51) inherits the app's @media (prefers-contrast: more) arm, which lifts --card-edge from 12% to 55% ink (demo/styles/foundation.css:270, :736). It is the counter-example that makes the file's three dead var(--destructive, oklch(…)) fallbacks and its hand-mixed 72% ink legible as defects rather than style.

Cross-axis: the corpus's own best work is L's attribution proof (challenge-L-library.md:76-79), which settled the owner's OM-5 question by geometry — pad: 4.8px 8.8px and pos: absolute uniquely identify DockStatusLamp.vue:56,44 against ApiOfflineChip.vue:49,42 — rather than by assertion. It is the one measurement in 1,601 lines of challenge prose I could not shake, and it is the load-bearing fact under the BLOCKER all three seats share.

The live text is demo/DESIGN.md:64-65: "Two mechanisms, both required wherever live numeric values render **at display scale**:" — D's block quote truncates the sentence at "render:" and drops the scope clause, then applies the law to an 11 px `text-micro` readout, the SMALLEST type rung in the app (glass-ui scale.css `--type-micro: 0.6875rem`). The law's own preamble (DESIGN.md:62-64) states the harm it forbids — "dragging any component slider from min to max changes NO containing card rect (±0px)" — and no card rect moves here: ConfiguratorRow's header is `flex items-baseline justify-between` over a full-width row (configurator-M5OaIlJd.js), so a width swing re-truncates the sibling label inside a fixed box; the Card (ConfigSliderPane.vue:99-102) is unaffected. The `ch`-reservation limb is additionally contra-indicated by the app's own history: readoutReservation.ts retired per-cell `ch` min-width reservation because it "rendered the worst case as BLANK width on every non-worst value — 39–51% of every cell was empty reservation" (quoted in this megatranche's codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:112, row M-21, ruled TRUE). The surviving obligation is the UNSCOPED sentence at VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:78, which binds mechanism 1 only — so D-7 stands as a tabular-figures finding and falls as a card-lock finding.

killed.claim: "Owner edict 5 violation (root-level styling, never per-instance override): a per-instance custom-property override that defeats the variant the same line requests" — and, in the design-system table, "`--slider-track-bg` per-instance override that defeats `variant="spectrum"` | the variant itself | violation (edict 5)".
killed.refutation: REFUTED IN PRODUCER BYTES, AND BY THE CORPUS'S OWN L AXIS. `--slider-track-bg` is not an override — it is the producer's PUBLISHED consumer hook, declared with a fallback in the recipe it is said to defeat: glass-ui.css `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-track { height: calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*1.5); background: var(--slider-track-bg, var(--secondary)) }` (and the base `.slider-track { background: var(--slider-track-bg, var(--muted-medium)) }`). Feeding it is the sanctioned door, exactly as challenge-L-library.md:448-451 concludes from the same bytes: "The `--slider-track-bg` feed on line 202 is *correct* by contrast: a custom-property handoff, not a selector reach. That is the pattern the other three should follow." Nor does it "defeat" the variant: the empty fill is the producer's own spectrum recipe — `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-range { -webkit-backdrop-filter:none; box-shadow:none; background:0 0 }` — and holds whatever the track feed is set to. The real defect, which D-5's other two points state correctly, is choosing `variant="spectrum"` (a chromatic-rail recipe that delegates the value signal to a consumer-supplied ramp) for a non-chromatic domain and then supplying no ramp.

killed.claim: "the promise is awaited and discarded, so a rejected clipboard write is an unhandled rejection with no user-visible result."
killed.refutation: FALSE — `writeClipboard` never rejects. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js:3-16: `async function r(e) { if (typeof navigator > "u" || !navigator.clipboard?.writeText) return { ok: !1, reason: "no-api" }; try { return await navigator.clipboard.writeText(e), { ok: !0 } } catch (e) { return console.warn("[useClipboard] clipboard writeText rejected:", e), { ok: !1, reason: "clipboard-api" } } }`. Every failure path returns a resolved result object, so awaiting-and-discarding cannot produce an unhandled rejection; the sibling axis states this correctly at challenge-C-implementation.md:343-346. The conclusion D draws (no user-visible result) survives via the correct mechanism — a discarded `{ok:false}` — but the named failure mode does not exist.

killed.claim: "31 sub-24 px targets; this pane *is* the app's tap-target outlier … WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 asks for ≥ 24×24 CSS px and has no pointer-type exemption; ConfigSliderPane.vue:218-230 gates its cure behind `@media (pointer: coarse)` and extends `block-size` only — the 12 px width is never addressed on any device."
killed.refutation: WRONG TARGET, AND THE EXCEPTION THAT APPLIES IS UNADDRESSED. (a) For a reka `Slider` the pointer target is the root/track, not the thumb: glass-ui.css gives the spectrum track `height: calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*1.5)` = 24 px, and the sibling axis's own census measured that element at 432×24 (challenge-D-design.md:273, `cls: "slider-track", rect: 432×24`) — which meets 24×24 in both dimensions. The 12 px figure is the visual thumb (`width: calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*.75)`), which PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:72 (§5 law 7) expressly separates from the operable target: "Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities. Accessibility floors do not require bloated visible chrome." (b) Even judging the thumb alone, SC 2.5.8's **Spacing** exception applies and BPC-6 never tests it: ConfigSliderPane.vue:215-217 sets `min-block-size: clamp(2rem, 7cqi, 2.625rem)` (32–42 px) per row, one thumb per row, so 24 px-diameter circles centred on adjacent thumbs cannot intersect. "No pointer-type exemption" is true and irrelevant — it is not the exemption in play. The proposed root-level cure would also inflate the producer's slider recipe for every consumer to fix a non-failure.

killed.claim: "**Propagation.** `geometry`/`surface`/`color` are re-spread into plain snapshot objects inside the computed, while `membrane`, `satellites` and `interaction` pass through as the live `reactive` proxy. The one slider that works (`membrane.smoothK`) is on the proxy side. … Both halves need the producer's read; the demo half is the snapshot."
killed.refutation: NOT ESTABLISHED, AND SELF-CONTRADICTING. The proxy/snapshot split is real in the bytes (HeroBlob.vue:152-178 spreads `geometry`, `surface`, `color` but passes `membrane`, `satellites`, `interaction` through the top-level spread as proxy references), but it does not predict the reported data: BPC's own table (challenge-C-implementation.md:29-30) shows the other two proxy-side atoms it tests, `warpAmp` and `noiseAmp`, at 5 px and 8 px — i.e. null — so 2 of 3 observations on the "working" side of the split refute the split as the explanation, and BPC concedes as much in the same paragraph before naming it a root anyway. It is also contradicted across axes: challenge-D-design.md:176 measures a SNAPSHOT-side atom (`surface.coreGlow`) at 6367 px / 4.91% while parked. The propagation mechanism additionally runs the wrong way for a snapshot: mutating `surface.coreGlow` DOES invalidate the computed (the spread reads that atom's keys), so a fresh config object reaches the prop, whereas mutating `membrane.warpAmp` does NOT invalidate it. Root 1 (construction) is arithmetic and stands; root 2 is a hypothesis presented as a finding. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

missed.claim: The entire "Pointer" section — all four sliders — tunes an interaction channel that has no pointer host anywhere in the app. This is a FOURTH, unnoticed root of the corpus's central BLOCKER, and it is pure source, needing no measurement.
missed.proof: BlobPane.vue:100-107 ships `interaction.pointerAttraction`, `pointerStrength`, `stretch`, `clickImpulse`. The producer binds the pointer field to a ref that is null unless the consumer opts in — node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/blob.js, Blob setup: `let … d = L("hitLayerRef"), f = w(() => !!t.pressLabel?.trim()), p = w(() => f.value && !t.disabled && !t.paused), m = w(() => p.value ? d.value : null), v = ve(m, { hitRadius: () => h })` — where `ve` is `useBlobPointer`, whose ONLY listeners are `e.addEventListener("pointermove", …)` / `"pointerleave"` on that same ref. The `.goo-blob-hit` button that would be that ref renders under `f.value ? … : T("", !0)`, i.e. only when `pressLabel` is a non-empty string. demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:13-19 passes `:color`, `:config`, `:paused`, `class` — and NO `pressLabel`; HeroBlob.vue:2-5 states the consequence in its own words: "Omitting pressLabel keeps the producer on its decorative canvas path—no button, focus target, **pointer host**, Tooltip, or duplicate Copy ownership." Belt and braces: HeroBlob.vue:10 wraps the whole thing in `<div class="pointer-events-none" aria-hidden="true">`, and glass-ui.css sets `.goo-blob-wrapper{…pointer-events:none;…}` and `.goo-blob-canvas{…pointer-events:none;…}`. So `m` is permanently null, no pointer listener is ever attached, `pointerActive` is永 false, and `clickImpulse` — driven by the hit button's `onClick: U` — has no emitter. `grep -rn "<Blob\b" demo` returns exactly one hit (HeroBlob.vue:13), so there is no other instance. CONSEQUENCE: combined with the four literal-overridden geometry atoms (D-3a/BPC-1/L-1), **8 of 31 sliders are provably inert from source alone**, before any idle-park or propagation argument. superlatives: Cross-package constant safety is airtight at BOTH ends. demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:381 does `reactive(structuredClone(BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS))` and demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:93 does `Object.assign(config, structuredClone(defaults))` — the shared glass-ui module constant is never aliased into app state and never mutated by a reset. Mutating an imported defaults object is one of the most common and most invisible bugs in this shape; neither site commits it, and the useAtmosphere comment (:379-380) states the reason ("structuredClone so the reactive copy owns deep atoms").

`reseedHeroStops` (demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:117-130) is a genuinely well-built seam: ONE function shared by the live-colour watch (:132) and the KeepAlive re-activation (:246-250), with the invariant stated at :113-116 — "both write the SAME palette shape into `heroStops` — the wake path can never diverge from the live path" — and a `try/catch` that leaves the LAST GOOD ramp on an unparseable colour rather than blanking or throwing. The published-surface discipline is real and mechanically enforced. vite.config.ts:37-50 GENERATES the self-alias set from `package.json#exports` using ANCHORED regexes, with a header that records the exact prior bug a string alias caused (`@mkbabb/value.js/math` prefix-rewritten into the `dist/value.js` FILE → "Not a directory" → the R-era boot break). Verified consequence: `grep -rn '@src/' demo/` (excluding the exempt `assets/docs` embeds) and `grep -rn 'from "[./]*\.\./src/' demo/` both return NOTHING. The demo can only consume the published surface, and the alias set cannot drift from it.

No leaks in the idle gate: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:227-230 `onScopeDispose` clears BOTH `idleTimer` and `poseTimer`, and the scrub detector windows its own buffer every tick (`changeTimes = changeTimes.filter(t => now - t <= SCRUB_WINDOW_MS)`, :270) so it cannot grow. Two of the three classic Vue timer/array leaks are pre-empted without ceremony.

`readPath` (demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:57-64) is null-safe on EVERY segment, not just the first: `if (cur == null || typeof cur !== "object") return undefined`. It is the reason a missing provider degrades to `undefined` instead of throwing inside the walk — and its care makes the write twin's asymmetry (L-11) conspicuous rather than symmetric sloppiness.

The `NumericAtomPath` guard (demo/scenes/blob/BlobPane.vue:19-52) is worth keeping even though BPC-4 is right that it has a hole. It DOES reject a typo and a boolean atom at compile time, and its comment reasons correctly and specifically about a subtle thing — that a homomorphic mapped type PRESERVES `?`, so indexing the mapped result injects `undefined` into the union, at BOTH nesting levels. That analysis is accurate for the `satelliteColors?`/`lightnessFloor?` leak it was written for (types.d.ts:115, :129). One token (`NonNullable<…>`) fixes the hole; the intent and the variance reasoning are better than anything else in this subtree.

demo/styles/foundation.css:648-698 is genuinely excellent design work: a documented two-tier `@media (forced-colors: active)` policy (U-F57 / BR-5) that refuses the blanket system-color substitution which would destroy a color tool's content, names a color-DISPLAY roster that keeps its real colors, leaves chrome at UA `auto` so it stays operable, and restores a system `Highlight` outline for focus because box-shadow rings cannot survive WHCM. Both URL/boot entry points are genuinely defensive. useColorUrl.ts:31-46 wraps parse+convert in try/catch and warns; hydrate.ts:98-130 falls through URL -> storage -> default on any throw, with a shape-validated localStorage read at :64-76. killed.claim: The mechanism of the Retry blank: "the availability latch is already tripped, so assertApiAttemptAllowed throws before any fetch; browsing returns to false within microtasks while the error leave is still in flight; out-in then holds isLeaving and the pending child never mounts. The faster the failure, the more certain the blank." (challenge-C-implementation.md:139-149)
killed.refutation: The symptom is confirmed; this causal chain is not established, and two of its consequences are wrong. (1) Vue 3.5.35 is built to recover from exactly this sequence: node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:1412-1419 sets `leavingHooks.afterLeave` to reset `state.isLeaving` and call `instance.update()`, `instance.update` still exists at :6190, and the DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT+transition case is special-cased in `remove` at :6659. I chased two candidate mechanisms and killed both: (a) EmptyState.vue's leading comment DOES compile to a two-root fragment (I compiled it with the installed @vue/compiler-sfc: patchFlag `2112 = STABLE_FRAGMENT|DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT`), but :6659 handles precisely that, and (b) a missing instance.update is not the case in 3.5.35. So a completed leave should re-render the error plate; why it does not is unproven. (2) The environment premise the mechanism rests on is contested inside the corpus: challenge-C-implementation.md:8-11/75-77 asserts localhost is latched by detectDevMisconfig so no request is issued, while challenge-D-design.md:537-549 measured VITE_API_URL SET on the same machine, and demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:112 confirms `if (i.viteApiUrlSet) return false;` — the latch cannot fire there. Where the latch does not fire the second Retry issues a real fetch and fails SLOWLY, which the stated mechanism predicts would NOT deadlock — yet the D axis reports the blanking anyway (challenge-D-design.md:72). Conclusion: the mechanism is not the latch's speed. Consequence for the cure list: moves 1 and 2 (one status-discriminated surface; drop mode="out-in") remain sound because they remove the deferred-mount state entirely; move 3 (make Retry a refresh, `isSort=true`) is also sound but for a reason the pass does not state — useBrowsePalettes.ts:63-69 shows isSort=true sets sortLoading and never touches `browsing`, so the keyed branch never flips at all.

killed.claim: "Neither origin that boots the client can reach the API: localhost is latched by detectDevMisconfig so no request is ever issued" — the premise the whole pass-3 apparatus is built on (challenge-C-implementation.md:8-11, 75-89).
killed.refutation: Environment-dependent and false wherever VITE_API_URL is set, which is the first line of the predicate: demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:112 `if (i.viteApiUrlSet) return false;` (the full triad is documented at :106-117 — unset VITE_API_URL AND loopback page AND cross-origin base). challenge-D-design.md:537-549 measured that exact configuration on this machine and recorded the console as an ordinary CORS-blocked fetch surfacing as ApiUnavailableError. The two governing axis documents therefore disagree about the reproduction environment. This does not touch pass 3's findings (all of which I re-derived statically or accepted as probe evidence), but any future seat re-running probe-C3/* must first read `import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL`, or it will misattribute which error species reaches the pane — and the pane's headline copy "The commons is unreachable." is CORRECT for ApiUnavailableError and wrong only for the DevMisconfig arm.

demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:6-11 documents a genuinely subtle Vue-compiler hazard at the exact site where it matters: the list comment is deliberately the div's FIRST CHILD because a leading comment node would make the component multi-root and PalettesPane's `$el` read for useSortable would resolve to the comment. I verified the hazard is real by compiling a sibling file with the installed toolchain — demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue's leading comment compiles to patchFlag 2112 (STABLE_FRAGMENT|DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT), i.e. a two-root component in dev. Someone here understood the compiler, wrote the reason down, and put the fix in the one file that needed it.

The transport's availability layer (demo/platform/transport/availability.ts:85-137) is a model of a designed degraded state: a pure, total, unit-testable predicate (`detectDevMisconfig`, :112-116) separating CORS-suicide from backend-down — two conditions the fetch layer collapses into one — plus a typed error per species and a 400-character message that names the exact command to run. That the pane throws all of it away at useBrowsePalettes.ts:79 (finding C-1) is the sharper indictment for how good the layer beneath it is.

demo/styles/foundation.css:653-696 and :830-841 declare ONE named colour-surface roster and reuse it across `forced-colors: active` and `@media print`, with the policy's intent written above it. Because the roster is one list with an `[data-color-surface]` extension point, D5-01 — the flagship defect on this component — has a one-line cure that fixes both media arms simultaneously. Centralising a policy so that its violations are cheap to repair is the whole point, and this file does it.

Resolution was proved in the same harness: `atoms.medium = { kind: "not-a-medium" }` errors TS2322 against the full 10-member union, and `const probe: string = atoms.medium` errors with the union's exact shape. TypeScript distributes over the discriminant, so the collapsed write is accepted. The ternary has no narrowing role; it is dead code, and D pass-1's D-13 and L's L-9 cure (`atoms.medium = { kind };`) are sound. C-17's INFO rationale for preserving the construct must not be carried forward.

killed.claim: "`--glass-accent` = `rgba(0,0,0,0)` (**DEFINED**, and transparent)" … "a **defined-but-transparent** `--glass-accent` (measured `rgba(0,0,0,0)` at `:root` in this app)".

This app declares `--glass-accent` nowhere: `grep -rn "glass-accent" demo/` → 0 hits. The definedness is the PRODUCER's own: `dist/styles/tokens/property-regs.css:1` registers `@property --glass-accent { syntax: "<color>"; inherits: true; initial-value: transparent; }`, and a registered property with an initial-value can never trigger `var()` fallthrough. That makes the defect universal — every glass-ui consumer that does not explicitly set `--select-dot-color` or `--glass-accent` ships an invisible selected state — rather than "any consumer under a transparent-accent root". Packet #4 must cite `property-regs.css:1`; a producer sent to look at this app's `:root` will find nothing there.

So P2-2's cure changes the affordance more than stated, and the 24×24 tap-target repair rests entirely on the `::before` inline-size term, not on the variant swap. (P2-C's core re-attribution — that the 12px inline extent is spectrum-only and therefore demo-chosen — is confirmed.)

superlatives: `demo/scenes/atmosphere/aurora-harmony-stops.ts` (40 lines, whole file) — the best idea in this component and one I have not seen elsewhere in the tree: every candidate harmony row previews the palette IT would resolve from the LIVE atoms, never a canned swatch. Its referent later drifted (C-2) — but the design instinct, and the fact that the file names the law it can be judged against, is why the defect is findable at all.

`demo/color-session/color-chips/PreviewStrip.vue` — `aria-hidden="true"` on a decorative specimen (`:39`), a `data-stops` stamp deliberately shared between chip and oracle (`:44`, `sample.ts:88-91`), a NAMED taste knob with its rejected alternative recorded inline (`STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP`, `:9-17`), honest truncation by mask-fade so a clipped palette reads as "continues" rather than as a complete palette it is not (`:73-75`), and a fixed golden proportion (`inline-size: 2.618rem` = φ²×1em, `:60-62`). Sixty lines that do everything right; the C axis's negative proofs 5 and 6 confirm it live.

`aurora-atoms.ts:15-52` — the `DEFAULT_AURORA_ATOMS` provenance block. Every constant carries the owner ruling that produced it, the bracket it landed inside, and the rejected alternative (the T-26 bracket closed from both sides; the T-32 rider's `scattered` prior with its measured x/y spreads). It records a real design invariant — the defaults carry NO `seed`, so Reset restores the SHAPE without disturbing the picked colour — which the C axis then verified live (negative proof 8). Documentation that makes an audit cheaper rather than longer.

`useAtmosphere.ts:283-290`, "THE NO-FIELD HONEST TERMINAL" — a degradation path that was DESIGNED rather than defaulted: on WebGL loss the persisted gradient ground IS the honest terminal, "never a blank canvas presented as a field", with a deliberate single re-arm on context-restore. This is the law C-1 correctly observes was written for the canvas and never extended to the controls — but the law itself is excellent, and it is why C-1 is expressible as a defect at all.

`ConfigSliderPane.vue:104-105` and `:159-162` — the W6-6 reasoning that moved the action bar OUT of the scroll region as a `flex-none` footer specifically so it can never occlude a slider or its readout. Second-order occlusion thinking of exactly the kind the enum block above it needed and did not get (D-2).

The corpus's own epistemic hygiene, which is above the norm and should survive the fold: challenge-D-design.md:287-355 is a standing "Corrections to pass 1" section that retires its predecessor's cure and kills its predecessor's `1/√φ` citation (correctly — I verified `PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:15` is Picker-scoped and `VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:78` names it the sole exception); challenge-C-implementation.md:622-627 records a HYPOTHESIS OF ITS OWN THAT WAS REFUTED (the `aria-label`-suppresses-value guess) with the raw CDP node as evidence, on the explicit ground that "a seat that only reports its confirmed guesses is not measuring."

killed.claim: "the component's own `aria-hidden="true"` (`EmptyState.vue:41`) is now redundant — glass-ui sets it."
killed.refutation: Wrong line and wrong conclusion. The attribute is at `EmptyState.vue:43`, on the trio **wrapper `<div>`** — a different element from the three producer `<span>`s that carry their own `aria-hidden`. It is not redundant, and it is load-bearing under test: `e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:74` asserts `await expect(trio).toHaveAttribute("aria-hidden", "true")` on `[data-slot="empty-state-trio"]`. Acting on this note reddens the oracle. The adjacent remark that "the comment at `:45-47` asserting a `div` host describes a `<span>`" also mis-cites: `:45-47` are the element lines; no comment there asserts a host.

killed.claim: "`| undefined` cancels `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` across this component's entire prop surface" (citing `tsconfig.base.json:13`); cure = "drop every `| undefined`, matching `ErrorBoundary`."
killed.refutation: Both limbs fail, and the cure would break the typecheck. (a) The flag is at `tsconfig.base.json:11`; line 13 is `useDefineForClassFields`. (b) The `| undefined` is load-bearing, not noise. `demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:38-44` declares its own props as `emptyText?: string; emptyEyebrow?: string; emptyHint?: string` — read as `string | undefined` — and forwards them at `:24-26` into `message`/`eyebrow`/`hint`. Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `string | undefined` is not assignable to a target `?: string`; TS's own diagnostic instructs "Consider adding 'undefined' to the types of the target's properties." Dropping `| undefined` introduces three type errors at exactly the wrapper the same report wants preserved until the split lands. `ErrorBoundary.vue:46-51` gets away with plain `?: string` because it has no forwarding consumer. Both other axes rule correctly and govern here: challenge-C-implementation.md:364 ("`?: T | undefined` on every prop is **correct**, not noise") and challenge-D-design.md:743-745 (N-4).

killed.claim: "The error register has THREE implementations, not two — `Markdown.vue:19-30` renders the register hand-replicated in a third file"; cure = "`Markdown.vue` composes the same `ErrorPlate`."
killed.refutation: Overstated as a clone and inverted as a cure. `demo/scenes/about/markdown/Markdown.vue:19-31` renders the **glass-ui `Alert` primitive** (`<Alert><AlertTitle …><AlertDescription …>`), imported from the barrel at `:35`. It has no `CircleAlert` glyph, no `detail` row, no action slot, no wrapper geometry, no `.plate-ink` — none of the five rows the axis's own EmptyState↔ErrorBoundary comparison table uses to establish a clone. killed.claim: "the promise is awaited and discarded, so a rejected clipboard write is an unhandled rejection with no user-visible result" — challenge-D-design.md:540-541.
killed.refutation: FALSE on both halves. `writeClipboard` never rejects: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useClipboard-D36OTaeT.js:3-15 returns `{ ok: false, reason: "no-api" }` when `navigator.clipboard?.writeText` is absent and wraps the write in try/catch, returning `{ ok: false, reason: "clipboard-api" }` on failure. And demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:88-90 DOES `await` inside an `async` handler, so even a rejection would surface as a handler rejection, not an unhandled one. BPC-10 (challenge-C-implementation.md:341-346) states the same facts correctly. What survives is the weaker, real claim: the `{ok, reason}` result is discarded and there is no success/failure surface — and the producer ships `useClipboard` with a `status` ref and an `onCopyError` hook (same file, :16-51) that is unused.

killed.claim: "The live readout violates the NORMATIVE card-lock law on both required mechanisms" — challenge-D-design.md:347, with the law quoted at :354-355 as "Two mechanisms, both required wherever live numeric values render:".
killed.refutation: The quotation is truncated in a way that changes the law's scope. demo/DESIGN.md:64-65 reads "Two mechanisms, both required wherever live numeric values render **at display scale**:" — D-7 drops "at display scale" and closes the sentence with a colon. The readout D-8 itself measures at 11 px `text-micro` (challenge-D-design.md:403) is not display scale. Mechanism 1 is separately refuted by the law's own text: DESIGN.md:71-72 says "Fira Code is tabular by default; Fraunces is NOT — a Fraunces-set number MUST declare `tabular-nums`", and D-8's own measurement records the readout as Fira Code. A missing declaration on a font that is tabular by default is not a violation of this law. The app's governing readout precedent cuts the same way: demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/readoutReservation.ts:6-13 records that per-cell `ch` `min-width` reservation was deliberately RETIRED ("the goal survives, the mechanism dies — no per-cell `ch` reservation returns"), a trade the mega-tranche already adjudicated as intentional (motion-quarantine.md M-21). What survives, and is real: there is no width reservation, and `fmt` (ConfigSliderPane.vue:84-86) genuinely swings 1↔5 characters (`fmt(2)==="2"`, `fmt(1.95)==="1.950"`). Charge that; do not charge a NORMATIVE double violation.

killed.id: D-5 (edict-5 limb) and D cure step 8
killed.claim: "Owner edict 5 violation (root-level styling, never per-instance override): a per-instance custom-property override that defeats the variant the same line requests" (challenge-D-design.md:300-301), cured by "Retire the track override. Delete `--slider-track-bg: var(--ink-muted…)`" (challenge-D-design.md:755-760).
killed.refutation: `--slider-track-bg` is a PRODUCER-PUBLISHED consumer hook, not a per-instance reach: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css reads it with fallbacks — `var(--slider-track-bg,var(--secondary))` and `var(--slider-track-bg,var(--muted-medium))`. Feeding a declared custom property is the documented door, which is exactly what L-8 says (challenge-L-library.md:448-451: "correct by contrast: a custom-property handoff, not a selector reach. That is the pattern the other three should follow"). The two axes contradict and L is right. The prescribed cure is worse than unsound — it regresses a landed accessibility gate. demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:190-201 records the measured pre-cure state ("the config sliders' spectrum TRACK computed `var(--secondary)` — ~1.09:1 light / 1.26:1 dark on the well … WCAG 1.4.11 wants ≥3:1") and names its born-RED gate; that gate is live at e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1162-1211, test "the ConfigSliderPane spectrum tracks ≥3:1 on the well (boot-A · M-34)", asserting `.config-console .configurator-row .slider-track` ≥ GRAPHICS_FLOOR. Deleting the override re-opens the exact defect. D-5's other limbs — a de-emphasis ink carrying the pane's dominant optical mass, and the track carrying no value information — stand as design findings; the edict-5 charge and the cure do not.

killed.id: L-1 / BPC-1 / D-3 — the prescribed `BLOB_HERO` cure
killed.claim: "the app config is seeded from `BLOB_HERO`, the hero renders `:config=\"appBlobConfig\"` unoverlaid" (challenge-C-implementation.md:101-103); "HeroBlob then selects the `hero` preset instead of hand-patching four keys" (challenge-L-library.md:163-164); "a real `<Blob>` bound directly to the injected `BLOB_CONFIG_KEY` object, with no prop override" (challenge-D-design.md:720-722).
killed.refutation: All three axes noticed that `BLOB_HERO` and the demo's inline register diverge and concluded "adopt the producer's" — none checked what adopting it costs. I read the installed preset: `BLOB_HERO.geometry.bodyRadius = 0.22`, not 0.325; `BLOB_HERO.surface.fissionAmp = 0`, not 0.6; `BLOB_HERO.color.paletteStops = ["#b5947f","#d4b27d","#dad6b1"]`, the canned brown. Adopting it whole regresses three separately witnessed decisions: (1) the W29 diameter contract, pinned by test/picker-blob-config.test.ts:26-27 `expect(radii).toEqual([0.325])` and `expect(2*radii[0]).toBeCloseTo(0.65, 12)`; (2) the WR-2/T-49c "never-meatball" fission arming documented at demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:134-150 (`HERO_FISSION_AMP = 0.6`, sized to the owner-ruled [0.4,0.8] bracket); (3) the live derived hero ramp (HeroBlob.vue:117-132), which the preset's baked stops would replace. The DEFECT (a preset authored as literals in a leaf; two divergent hero registers) stands at full BLOCKER weight. The CURE as written does not — a correct transposition has to push the demo's three deltas INTO the producer preset (or into a named second preset) first, not swap the consumer onto the existing one.

killed.claim: "`geometry`/`surface`/`color` are re-spread into plain snapshot objects inside the computed, while `membrane`, `satellites` and `interaction` pass through as the live `reactive` proxy. The one slider that works (`membrane.smoothK`) is on the proxy side." — challenge-C-implementation.md:90-95.
killed.refutation: The reactivity is exactly inverted. In demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:152-178 the nested spreads `...appBlobConfig.geometry` (:161), `...appBlobConfig.surface` (:170) and `...appBlobConfig.color` (:171) READ every leaf of those three atoms, so each leaf is a tracked dependency of the computed — a write to `surface.coreGlow` or `color.hueRange` or `geometry.satelliteCount` DOES invalidate `heroConfig` and mint a fresh prop object. By contrast the top-level `...appBlobConfig` (:153) reads only the KEYS `membrane`/`satellites`/`interaction`; their leaves are never read, so a write to `membrane.smoothK` or `interaction.pointerAttraction` mints nothing. The "snapshot" side is the side that propagates through the prop; the "proxy" side is the side that does not. The inversion matters because HeroBlob.vue:63-66 states the wake contract in terms of object identity ("Blob's liveConfig() re-reads the prop, so the fresh computed object is exactly the wake-repaint shape the producer built for") — see the missed finding.

killed.claim: "WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 asks for ≥ 24×24 CSS px and has **no pointer-type exemption**" — challenge-C-implementation.md:251-254.
killed.refutation: True as to pointer type, but SC 2.5.8's governing exception here is Spacing, which BPC-6 never addresses. Under Spacing, undersized targets conform when a 24 CSS-px-diameter circle centred on each does not intersect another target's circle. demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:215-217 sets the row rhythm to `min-block-size: clamp(2rem, 7cqi, 2.625rem)` = 32–42 px, and each row carries exactly one target, so on BPC-6's own measured geometry (12 × 24 thumbs, one per row, ≥32 px apart) the 24 px circles do not intersect and the pane plausibly CONFORMS. The 12 px thumb width and the block-only coarse-pointer extension (:222-229 sets `block-size` and `inset-inline: 0`, never an inline dimension) are real and worth a density/ergonomics finding; "31 SC 2.5.8 failures" is not established, and the cure (an unconditional 24 px inline hit area in the producer's slider recipe) needs a spacing argument it does not make.

killed.claim: "the 35 sliders are not rendered" on mobile (challenge-L-library.md:359-361); "`readPath` returns `undefined` for all 35 rows" (challenge-L-library.md:541-542); "55 operable controls, 35 sliders" (challenge-L-library.md:45-46).

killed.claim: "4 of 5 Geometry sliders **+ fissionAmp** inert; pane readout ≠ rendered blob" — challenge-L-library.md:614.
killed.refutation: BlobPane exposes no `surface.fissionAmp` slider. The "Lit Glass" section (BlobPane.vue:88-97) is specStrength, specShininess, rimStrength, rimPower, iridescence, sssScale, coreGlow — `fissionAmp` is absent, as D-12 and BPC-12 correctly report (it is one of the 8 unreachable numeric atoms). HeroBlob.vue:170 does override it, but there is no pane control for the override to render inert. The row conflates the L-1 family with the opposite finding.

missed.claim: `heroConfig` mints a heterogeneous object: `geometry`/`surface`/`color` are tracked snapshots while `membrane`/`satellites`/`interaction` are untracked live proxies — so 13 of BlobPane's 31 sliders can never produce the fresh prop object the demo's own wake contract depends on.
missed.proof: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:152-178. The computed's dependency set is: every top-level key via `...appBlobConfig` (:153), plus every leaf of `geometry` (:161), `surface` (:170) and `color` (:171) via the nested spreads, plus `heroStops` (:171) and `isLgViewport` (:177). It does NOT include a single leaf of `membrane`, `satellites` or `interaction` — those are read only at the key level, so their objects pass through by reference and a write to them never invalidates the computed and never changes the `config` prop's identity. HeroBlob.vue:63-66 states the contract in exactly those terms: "the producer's own `config ?? injectedConfig` seam; Blob's liveConfig() re-reads the prop, so **the fresh computed object is exactly the wake-repaint shape** the producer built for". By that contract, the 7 Membrane rows (BlobPane.vue:68-74), the 4 Pointer rows (:102-105) and the 2 Satellites rows (:111-112) — 13 of 31 — cannot mint that shape and therefore cannot wake a parked renderer; they take effect only for as long as the loop is already running and only if the engine re-reads per frame. This is the structural half of BPC-2 that no axis stated, and BPC-1's root-2 states it backwards (see killed). It also explains why C's own probe11 table shows Warp/Noise Amp/Attraction pinned at 5-8 px alongside the snapshot-side atoms: two different failure paths, one symptom.

missed.claim: `geometry.satelliteRadius`'s shipped default 0.082 is off the slider's own step grid, so the user can never return to it by any slider interaction.
missed.proof: demo/scenes/blob/BlobPane.vue:60 declares `s("geometry.satelliteRadius", "Sat Radius", 0.02, 0.20, 0.005)`; the installed `BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS.geometry.satelliteRadius = 0.082` (read directly from @mkbabb/glass-ui/blob-config). `(0.082 − 0.02) / 0.005 = 12.4` — not an integer. Delete `--slider-track-bg: var(--ink-muted…)` and let the `spectrum` variant paint what it declares — a real `.slider-range` restores the value signal … and makes the WHCM roster entry at foundation.css:693 protect something that exists. Kills D-5, D-6." (challenge-D-design.md:755-760)
killed.refutation: STRUCTURALLY UNSOUND AND REGRESSIVE. (1) Deleting the feed falls the track back to `var(--secondary)` — which demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:190-201 records as the born-RED O-18 defect this exact line was landed to cure: "the config sliders' spectrum TRACK computed `var(--secondary)` — ~1.09:1 light / 1.26:1 dark on the well, an invisible control extent (WCAG 1.4.11 wants ≥3:1)". The cure would re-open a graphics-contrast failure. (2) The spectrum variant does NOT "declare" a painted range — glass-ui.css sets `.slider-range{background:0 0}` under `[data-variant=spectrum]`, so no fill would appear and no value signal would be restored. (3) It therefore also cannot fix D-6: the roster entry would still protect a transparent element. The sound cure is the opposite move — drop `variant="spectrum"` for non-chromatic axes so the default recipe's `.slider-range` (`--liquid-fill-tint`, `--liquid-fill-blur`) paints a filled/unfilled split, which simultaneously stops the pane wearing the `data-variant="spectrum"` attribute that mis-aims the WHCM roster.

killed.claim: "Mechanism 1 absent, on every row … readoutFVN [\"normal\"] … Every other live-number surface in the app declares it — the Blob console is the exception." (challenge-D-design.md:350-367)
killed.refutation: REFUTED by the law D-7 itself cites. demo/DESIGN.md:69-70: "Fira Code is tabular by default; Fraunces is NOT — a Fraunces-set number MUST declare `tabular-nums`." The Blob readout is set in the mono face — ConfiguratorRow renders `name` as `text-micro font-mono …` (glass-ui dist configurator-M5OaIlJd.js) and demo/styles/utils.css:9-11 maps `--font-mono`; a monospaced face is tabular by construction. `font-variant-numeric: normal` is the correct computed value for a font whose default figures are already tabular; it is not evidence of proportional figures. The width swing D measured ("3" 6.8px → "0.220" 33.9px) is a CHARACTER-COUNT change, which tabular figures do not and cannot address.

killed.id: D-7 quotation of the NORMATIVE card-lock law
killed.claim: "Two mechanisms, **both required** wherever live numeric values render" (challenge-D-design.md:352, quoting demo/DESIGN.md:60-79 as NORMATIVE)
killed.refutation: MISQUOTED — the scope qualifier is elided behind the ellipsis. demo/DESIGN.md:64-65 reads: "Two mechanisms, both required wherever live numeric values render **at display scale**". The Blob console readout is `text-micro` (11px), the smallest rung in the ladder — the opposite of display scale. The law's operative promise, "a value change may never move the card: dragging any component slider from min to max changes NO containing card rect (±0px)" (DESIGN.md:62-64), is not breached either: the Card is `h-full` inside a fixed pane slot (ConfigSliderPane.vue:99-102), so no card rect moves. What survives is intra-row text-box reflow — real, but MINOR, not a NORMATIVE breach.

killed.claim: "reserve `max legal ch` per definition" (challenge-D-design.md:751-752) / "`ch` worst-case reservation — mechanism 2 absent, on every row" (challenge-D-design.md:361)
killed.refutation: PRESCRIBES A RETIRED MECHANISM. demo/picker/display/ColorComponentDisplay/readoutReservation.ts:5-13 records the landed ruling: "The retired mechanism — every cell reserving its worst-case `ch` as `min-width` — rendered the worst case as BLANK width on every non-worst value (39–51% of every cell was empty reservation, pooling between the values as the owner's 'spread apart' dead air, shot t-2002-52/t-2002-09). Cells are now INTRINSIC and the card-lock GOAL is re-earned at tuple/line level (R4: the goal survives, the mechanism dies — **no per-cell `ch` reservation returns**)." Independently corroborated by the formation's own quarantine sweep, motion-quarantine.md row M-21, which grades the same trade-off TRUE and superlative-aware. The residual true defect is `fmt` (ConfigSliderPane.vue:84-86) switching the number's KIND mid-drag (1↔5 chars); the sanctioned cure is a fixed per-definition precision on `SliderDef`, not `ch` reservation.

killed.claim: "31 sub-24 px targets; this pane *is* the app's tap-target outlier … WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 asks for ≥ 24×24 CSS px and has no pointer-type exemption; ConfigSliderPane.vue:218-230 gates its cure behind `@media (pointer: coarse)` and extends `block-size` only — the 12 px width is never addressed on any device." (challenge-C-implementation.md:239-258)
killed.refutation: MIS-MEASURES THE TARGET. 12×24 is the thumb GLYPH, not the region that accepts a pointer action. node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Slider/SliderImpl.js:46-52 handles `onPointerdown` on the slider root and, when the target is not a thumb, emits `slideStart` — the whole rail is click-to-jump operable. The spectrum recipe sizes that rail at `glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-track{height:calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*1.5)}` = 24px tall at full row width (D's own census measured it 432×24, challenge-D-design.md:273). So the SC 2.5.8 target is 432×24 and passes on fine pointers. On coarse pointers ConfigSliderPane.vue:222-229 lifts it further with `inset-inline: 0` (FULL inline, not block-only as C claims) and `block-size: max(100%, var(--dock-touch-target, 2.75rem))` = 44px. The "39 small tap targets" figure in the visual REPORT counts glyph rects, not targets. Downgrade MAJOR → INFO.

killed.claim: "`shots/forced-colors-desktop/blob.png` is **not a forced-colors capture** — it renders the full chromatic palette … which WHCM substitution would have flattened … The stored frame should be re-captured or struck." (challenge-D-design.md:45-49)
killed.refutation: REFUTED by the frame itself, read against its light-mode sibling. Relative to shots/safari-desktop-light/blob.png, the forced-colors frame has the glass blur, surface tints and drop shadows STRIPPED (both cards flatten to Canvas cream), and the two cards, the dock and BOTH `Copy JSON` / `Reset` buttons gain hard 1px borders they do not otherwise have — textbook WHCM. The surviving chroma is precisely what the roster at demo/styles/foundation.css:685-696 exempts (`.goo-blob-canvas`, `[data-color-surface]`, the gradient/readout rails, `.watercolor-swatch`) plus the ambient field. The frame is valid evidence and should NOT be struck — and it materially contradicts D-6's own consequence limb (see `unproven`).

killed.claim: "The section heading is … set in the *mono* family. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4 assigns section heading → `text-heading` → Plus Jakarta Sans, and reserves Fira Code for 'value, code, or provenance'. The matrix is declared 'closed across all eighteen compositions' with exactly one named exception (P019's Picker pair). This is a second, undeclared exception." (challenge-D-design.md:407-412)
killed.refutation: REFUTED ON THE FAMILY LIMB, RE-AIMED ON THE SIZE LIMB. (a) VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4's own value row reads "`text-mono-small`, **or the already-established `mono-caption` where the content is a caption**" — an uppercase tracked mono eyebrow is the admitted caption idiom, not a new exception. (b) glass-ui's own shipped section-heading recipe is mono: `.section-label { @apply text-mono-caption; color: var(--muted-foreground); }` and `text-mono-caption{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:var(--type-caption);letter-spacing:var(--type-tracking-caps);text-transform:uppercase}`. `.config-section-title` (ConfigSliderPane.vue:237-243) is a byte-for-byte hand-roll of that recipe EXCEPT for the size: it declares `font-size: var(--type-small)` (16.4px at 1440) where the producer utility declares `--type-caption` (clamp(0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem) ≈ 14.4px at 1440). The defect is the RUNG and its cause is the re-roll, not the family. D's size observation (16.4px = 16.4px, no rung between furniture and content) is correct and survives; its "do no hierarchical work" conclusion is overstated — in all three captures the headers read clearly as headers via case, tracking, colour and the hairline. See MISSED M5.

killed.claim: D: "the scroll port (`.pane-scroll-fade` vs the producer's `FadingScroll`)" (challenge-D-design.md:246-247, and the design-system boundary row at :646). L: "scroll port with fade | `scrollMode=\"auto\"` → `FadingScroll` | `.pane-scroll-fade scrollbar-thin` (`:106`)" (challenge-L-library.md:191).
killed.refutation: BOTH AXES ASSUMED A FADE THAT DOES NOT EXIST. `.pane-scroll-fade` is declared exactly once, in the unscoped block at demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:54-57, and declares only `contain: layout style paint;` and `scroll-timeline: --pane-scroll block;`. There is no `mask-image`, no gradient, no scroll shadow anywhere on it — the only mask in that file is at PaneHeader.vue:91 and belongs to `.pane-header::before` (the header veil's 14px feather). So the demo did not hand-roll a lower-fidelity fading scroll port; it hand-rolled a scroll-timeline host whose NAME and whose consumer comment (ConfigSliderPane.vue:103-105, "The scroll region owns the fade mask + overflow") both assert a fade that is absent. This flips a design-system-duplication finding into an unhandled-overflow finding — see MISSED M3.

missed.claim: WRONG PRODUCER PRIMITIVE, against an explicit producer directive: ConfiguratorRow is contra-indicated for accessible form controls, and glass-ui ships `LabeledField` for exactly this. All three axes graded the ConfiguratorRow usage "✅ correct".
missed.proof: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/configurator/ConfiguratorRow.vue.d.ts:40-49 — "**ConfiguratorRow** (this) — for TOKEN, PRESET controls. Carries the token-`name` reference, the opt-in `reset` affordance (`canReset`), and the three-rung `size` axis. **No a11y for/id wiring.** — **LabeledField** — for form controls. Carries stable label, description, error, requirement, state, and layout associations without styling the control. **Reach for ConfiguratorRow only when token metadata or reset is the content; use LabeledField directly for an accessible form control, including inside a Configurator.**" glass-ui 7.0.0 publishes `./labeled-field` (package.json exports; dist/components/labeled-field/). demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:137-153 wraps 31 sliders in ConfiguratorRow. Two measurable consequences, both already visible in the corpus but mis-rooted: (a) the compiled row renders its label as `<Label class="truncate text-small font-medium text-foreground">` with NO `for` attribute passed (glass-ui dist configurator-M5OaIlJd.js — only `class` is bound), and `LabelProps.for` is optional (Label.vue.d.ts:4), so the pane emits 31 ORPHAN `<label>` elements — e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:950 confirms they are real `label` elements. Clicking the visible label does not focus or operate its slider, and the name must be hand-duplicated as `aria-label` (ConfigSliderPane.vue:145) — which is the mechanism that makes D-9's duplicate-name defect possible at all. (b) The live value is put in `name`, a mono TOKEN-REFERENCE rung, which is the real cause of D-8 limb 2's 11px readout and of M4 below. Contradicted grade: challenge-D-design.md:652 files this row as "✅ correct"; challenge-L-library.md:198-200 praises it as the one thing the demo composes correctly.

missed.claim: The seven section titles have zero semantic representation — no heading, no group, no association. To assistive technology the pane is a flat run of 31 identically-shaped sliders, two pairs of which share a name.
missed.proof:
demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:123-130 — the group wrapper is `
` with no `role="group"` and no `aria-labelledby`; the title is `
{{ section.title }}
` — a `span` inside a `div`, no heading element, no `id`. Nothing in the pane emits a heading below PaneHeader's `

`. The visual grouping is carried entirely by a hairline (:232-235) and a colour/case shift (:237-243), neither of which reaches the accessibility tree. challenge-D-design.md:441-443 notices the symptom in passing ("a section header that is neither sticky nor programmatically associated") but files it only as supporting text for the duplicate-label MINOR; challenge-D-design.md:729-733 offers the semantics only as a by-product of adopting `ConfiguratorLayer` (which ships `role=button`+`aria-expanded`+`aria-controls`, ConfiguratorLayer.vue.d.ts:27). No axis files the missing group semantics as a defect in its own right, and it is independently fixable without adopting the layer.

missed.claim: A 3.76-screen console with NO overflow affordance of any kind, and an in-source comment that asserts one that does not exist. The pane's own title and description scroll away permanently.
missed.proof: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:103-105 comment: "The scroll region owns the fade mask + overflow". The class it applies (:106 `pane-scroll-fade scrollbar-thin flex-1 min-w-0 overflow-y-auto overflow-x-hidden`) is declared once, at demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:54-57, and contains ONLY `contain: layout style paint` and `scroll-timeline: --pane-scroll block` — no `mask-image`, no gradient, no scroll shadow (the file's only mask, PaneHeader.vue:91, belongs to `.pane-header::before`). There are no sticky section headers (`.config-section-header` at :232-235 declares no `position`), no scroll-progress affordance and no section nav. Visible in audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/blob.png: the `Warp` row's rail is hard-clipped at the well's bottom edge with no gradient. Compounding: `PaneHeader` is placed INSIDE the scroll region (ConfigSliderPane.vue:106-107), so "Blob" and its description leave the viewport permanently after the first screen — the pane loses its identity for 2.76 of its 3.76 screens. challenge-D-design.md:211-226 counts the screens and charges the absence of disclosure, but treats the scroll port as an existing (if lower-fidelity) fading port; challenge-L-library.md:191 does the same. Neither notices there is no fade.

missed.claim: The 31 live values are not a column: each number's x-origin is a function of its label's length, so the pane's entire numeric content cannot be scanned, compared, or read as a set.
missed.proof:
ConfiguratorRow's header is `
` containing `
[label][sub][name]
` (glass-ui dist configurator-M5OaIlJd.js, vnodes `Q` and `ne`) — label and value are glued left in one inner flex, and `justify-between` pushes only the optional reset button right. ConfigSliderPane.vue:141 puts the live value in that `name` slot. Result, visible in all three captures (shots/safari-desktop-light/blob.png, safari-desktop-dark/blob.png, forced-colors-desktop/blob.png): `Body Radius 0.220`, `Satellites 3`, `Sat Radius 0.082`, `Orbit Radius 0.170`, `Eccentricity 0.050` begin at five different x positions. This is the correct placement for a token reference (what `name` is documented as, ConfiguratorRow.vue.d.ts:63) and the wrong placement for a value column. It is also what makes D-7's 1↔5 character `fmt` swing legible as jitter rather than as an in-place re-ink — i.e. the ragged column is upstream of the finding D filed. Same root as M1.

missed.claim: `.config-section-title` re-rolls a shipped glass-ui utility at the wrong type rung — which is the direct cause of the size collision D-8 filed against the wrong target.
missed.proof: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:237-243 hand-authors `font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--type-small); text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: var(--tracking-caps); color: var(--muted-foreground)`. glass-ui already ships that exact recipe: `.section-label { @apply text-mono-caption; color: var(--muted-foreground); }` over `text-mono-caption{font-family:var(--font-mono);font-size:var(--type-caption);letter-spacing:var(--type-tracking-caps);text-transform:uppercase}`. The single divergence is the size: `--type-small` (clamp(0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1.25rem) = 16.4px at 1440) instead of `--type-caption` (clamp(0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem) ≈ 14.4px), and 16.4px is exactly the row label's `text-small` — hence no rung. demo/DESIGN.md:50-51 names `.section-label` among the utilities to use "instead of raw `text-2xl` etc.", and demo/styles/utils.css:13-17 already builds `.section-subtitle` on top of it for the gradient/mix/generate control bars — so the demo knows the utility and this one site declined it. Owner edicts 4 and 5. No axis names `.section-label`.

missed.claim: A 5-value discrete axis is drawn as a continuous rail, and the pane has no control vocabulary for non-continuous domains at all.
missed.proof: BlobPane.vue:59 `s("geometry.satelliteCount", "Satellites", 0, 4, 1)` renders through the identical path as BlobPane.vue:70 `s("membrane.noiseAmp", "Noise Amp", 0.0, 0.10, 0.001)` — same `<Slider variant="spectrum">` (ConfigSliderPane.vue:144-152), same uniform rail, no ticks, no detents, no stepper, and (per the producer's spectrum recipe, `.slider-range{background:0 0}`) no fill. Visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/blob.png: "Satellites 3" is communicated by a 12px thumb sitting at ~75% of a 432px rail with nothing marking the four legal positions. The pane also has no control for the two shipped enums (`membrane.merge` types.d.ts:100, `quality` types.d.ts:220) or the two booleans (`surface.lit` :133, `surface.shadow` :139) — and the mechanism for enum rows exists in the same component and is used by the sibling pane (ConfigSliderPane.vue:110 `<slot />`; demo/scenes/atmosphere/AuroraPane.vue:117-160). challenge-D-design.md:449-457 (D-10) files the bipolar-vs-unipolar case and challenge-D-design.md:507 notes the enums are absent, but no axis notices that a discrete integer count is being drawn as a continuous quantity.

missed.claim: 31 raw shader-uniform labels with zero explanatory text, on rows whose producer ships two unused props for exactly that, while the pane's single sentence of prose is spent restating its own section titles.
missed.proof:
BlobPane.vue:68-105 — "Smooth K", "Warp", "Rim Power", "Sub-surface", "Core Glow", "Eccentricity", "Click Impulse", "Shininess" are uniform names lifted from the shader with no gloss. ConfiguratorRow ships `sub?: string` ("Use `sub` for a descriptive secondary label", ConfiguratorRow.vue.d.ts:59-65) and `description?: string` ("Optional helper, value description (below the control)", :66) — the producer even renders `description` as `

` (dist configurator-M5OaIlJd.js vnode `$`). ConfigSliderPane's `SliderDef` (:27-33) carries neither, so no consumer can supply either. Meanwhile the pane's one sentence, BlobPane.vue:128, restates four of its seven section titles (the finding D-15 files at challenge-D-design.md:559-566). PROPORTION-AUDIT §5 law 6, "Subtraction precedes explanation", is cited by D against that sentence — the sharper reading is that the explanation is in the wrong place: deleted from the description, absent from the rows that need it.

missed.claim: The satellite domain is split across two sections, one of which does not contain four of its six axes.
missed.proof: BlobPane.vue:59-62 puts `satelliteCount`, `satelliteRadius`, `orbitRadius` and `eccentricity` under "Geometry"; BlobPane.vue:108-114 creates a section literally titled "Satellites" containing only `mergeDuration` and `emergeDuration`. A user hunting satellite behaviour finds a two-row section that omits the count, the size and the orbit. The abbreviation is inconsistent inside one screen ("Sat Radius" at :60 vs "Satellites" at :59 and :109), and "Tempo" (:115-118) is a section of one. The producer's docblock names the intended blob grouping — "blob has Mood / Body / Surface / Color / Motion / Pointer / Render" (ConfiguratorLayer.vue.d.ts:6-7) — which is neither this taxonomy nor this granularity. challenge-D-design.md:216 lists the seven titles as evidence of flatness but does not examine whether the partition is correct.

missed.claim: 31 unskippable tab stops with no grouping, no landmark and no section navigation stand between the pane's entry and its two actions.
missed.proof: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:106-157 is the scroll region (31 sliders, each a `tabindex=0` `role=slider` per the producer's Slider); :163-174 places the `Copy JSON` / `Reset` dock AFTER it in DOM order as a flex-none footer. Tab order is therefore header → 31 sliders → Copy → Reset, with no skip link, no `role="group"` boundaries to jump by (M2), no collapsible layers (D-4) and no landmark inside the pane. Combined with the absent reset announcement (challenge-C-implementation.md:333-341 measures zero `aria-live` on `.config-console`) a keyboard user traverses 3.76 screens to reach a destructive action that then reports nothing. The footer's placement itself is correct and deliberate (see superlatives); the defect is that nothing was added to make the 31-stop thicket navigable.

unproven: D-6 CONSEQUENCE LIMB — "Under forced colors the track becomes invisible … track: rgb(255,255,255) — identical to the well … The entire 31-control surface loses its control extent" (challenge-D-design.md:307-322). Single-engine (Chromium `forcedColors: "active"`, probe 8) and CONTRADICTED by the corpus's own WebKit arm: in audit/visual/shots/forced-colors-desktop/blob.png — which is a genuine WHCM capture (glass, tints and shadows stripped; hard borders minted on both cards, the dock and both footer buttons; see `killed`) — all seven visible tracks render as clearly separated dark slabs against a cream well. Needs a two-engine re-measure before any gate binds. The MECHANISM limb (roster mis-aim at foundation.css:685-696) is confirmed statically and stands on its own.

D-3(b) / BPC-2 / L-1 second reproduction — the idle-park findings ("five of six full-range sweeps produced a byte-identical frame", challenge-D-design.md:166-201; "three .goo-blob-canvas captures are byte-identical", challenge-C-implementation.md:109-131; "four byte-identical PNGs", challenge-L-library.md:114-131). The MECHANISM is confirmed in source and needs no probe: demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:211-212 sets `BLOB_IDLE_MS = 2000` / `SLEEPY_POSE_MS = 3300`, and `noteBlobActivity()` (:216) has exactly three callers — `onActivated` (:248), the `cssColorOpaque` watch (:264-280) and the `savedColorStrings.length` watch (:286-295). No config write is in that set. The PIXEL DELTAS are live-only and I did not re-run them.

D-2's 35.2:1 form-to-preview area ratio and the 1,141,739 px² / 32,468 px² rects (challenge-D-design.md:102-109); D-5's measured track colour `oklch(0.447121 0.00386159 34.63)` on a well of `oklab(0.913295 0.0055 0.0130)` (challenge-D-design.md:266-268); D-4's `scrollH 2611 / screens 3.76` (challenge-D-design.md:214-215). All live-only numbers. The structural claims each supports are confirmed from source and from the stored captures; the figures themselves are UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE for this seat.

FOCUS VISIBILITY — challenge-D-design.md:605 records in its state matrix, but declines to file, "focus is a 2 px box-shadow at 30% alpha (`color(srgb 0.6655 0.0001 0.2617 / 0.3)`) over a near-black track … barely separable from the thumb outline". The ring is token-driven and producer-owned (glass-ui.css: `glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-thumb:focus-visible{box-shadow:var(--focus-ring-shadow),var(--shadow-sm);outline:none}`), and `--ink-muted` is JS-stamped at boot (demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:317-329), so whether the ring clears WCAG 2.4.11 / 1.4.11 against the painted track in either scheme is not decidable statically. D's restraint here was correct; the question is open and should be measured, not carried.

BPC-1 PROPAGATION ROOT — "`geometry`/`surface`/`color` are re-spread into plain snapshot objects while `membrane`, `satellites` and `interaction` pass through as the live reactive proxy … the producer's uniform re-pack covers `smoothK` and not [`warpAmp`, `noiseAmp`]" (challenge-C-implementation.md:90-95). The spread asymmetry is real in source (HeroBlob.vue:160-177), but the claim about which uniforms the producer re-packs is inferred from pixel deltas and requires reading the engine's uniform path or a live probe. Note it is in tension with challenge-L-library.md:96-99, which measured `membrane.warpAmp` as passing through cleanly ('Warp | 1 | 1 | passes ✔').

D-3's live-window jitter normalisation (challenge-D-design.md:189-201) — the 'below noise floor' verdicts for Body Radius and Eccentricity are derivative of the source override already confirmed in D-3(a), so nothing turns on them; recorded as live-only rather than re-run.
superlatives: EXACT CENSUS — challenge-D-design.md:473-521 (D-12). I re-derived the entire leaf inventory independently from node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/blob/types.d.ts:81-222 and D's two sets match element for element: 39 numeric leaves, 31 exposed, the 8 unexposed numeric (`canvasSize`, `lightnessFloor`, `shadowSoftness`, `iridHue`, `iridSpeed`, `sssPower`, `fissionAmp`, `morphT`) and the 9 unexposed non-numeric (`absorbedDuration`, `orbitDuration`, `membrane.merge`, `paletteStops`, `lit`, `shadow`, `rimColor`, `lightDir`, `quality`). Its diagnosis of the guard as "an exhaustiveness guard pointed the wrong way" (challenge-D-design.md:514-520) is the sharpest single sentence in the corpus and is correct.

NEGATIVE PROOFS PUBLISHED AGAINST THE AUTHOR'S OWN THESIS — challenge-L-library.md:316-330 and :414-422. L-5 and L-7 each built the finding, then measured the bundle cost through the real toolchain, got byte-identical output, and printed it: "**Byte-identical.** Rollup tree-shakes the renderer barrel away completely. The production bundle pays nothing; the claim is a boundary claim, not a size claim" and "**No perf defect** — this is purely a legacy-structure defect, and it should be reported as such, not dressed up as bloat." That is exactly the discipline this seat exists to reward, and it is why L-5/L-7 survive re-reading intact when louder findings do not.

PRE-EMPTIVE NEGATIVE EVIDENCE — challenge-C-implementation.md:387-407 (BPC-13, "checked, sound — do not re-litigate"). Its range/default coherence claim is verifiable and holds: every `[min,max]` triple at BlobPane.vue:58-117 brackets the shipped `BLOB_CONFIG_DEFAULTS` value, so there is no clamp-on-mount and no silent write. Publishing the checks that FAILED to become findings saved this pass real budget and is the correct shape for a challenge document.

THE PRODUCT — demo/picker/visual/HeroBlob.vue:81-111, `floorStops()`. A closed-form, two-branch, zero-iteration ΔL ink floor with an explicit budget constraint stated in the source ("CLOSED-FORM inside the 12ms drag headroom … an iterative solve here is forbidden"), a documented headroom flip when the chosen side has none (:107-108), and a booked producer replacement (`lightnessFloor`, :90-92). missed.claim: MAJOR — a library correctness bug in the shipped artifact: pure white cannot be converted to HSL. `convertColor(rgb(255,255,255),"hsl")` returns `color_non_finite`, because the saturation division runs BEFORE the powerless law can fire. In the demo this throws through `valueOrThrow` inside a watcher and desynchronises the model.
missed.proof: MEASURED: a 0..255 grey sweep to hsl fails at exactly one input — `255: color_non_finite` — while hsv passes for all 256 and the immediate neighbours are fine (rgb(255,255,254)->hsl ok, rgb(254,255,255)->hsl ok). Mechanism, src/color/anchors.ts:173: `return [hsv[0], delta === 0 ? 0 : delta / (1 - Math.abs(2 * lightness - 1)), lightness];` — for white the XYZ round trip yields max/min straddling 1.0 so `lightness === 1` exactly while `delta` is ~4e-16 non-zero, giving `4e-16 / 0 = Infinity`. src/color/operations.ts:38 then calls `isPowerless("hsl", channels)` on that Infinity: `Infinity * 0` is NaN, `NaN === 0` is false, so the powerless law that exists precisely for this case never triggers, and `makeColor` rejects the non-finite channel. The guard is in the wrong order — the powerless test must precede the division. Demo consequence: white + select HSL -> ColorPicker.vue:352 `updateToColorSpace("hsl")` -> useColorPipeline.ts:171 `convertPickerColor` -> picker-color.ts:104-107 `valueOrThrow` throws inside a watcher callback, so `selectedColorSpace` is already 'hsl' while `model.color.space` is still 'rgb' -> ComponentSliders.vue:131 then asks for an 'h' channel of an rgb colour -> picker-color.ts:154 `Unknown rgb channel: h`. Also observed in the same sweep: rgb(255,255,254)->hsl returns s = 1.000000000000085, outside the declared 0–1 domain.

superlatives: The published-surface discipline is right BY CONSTRUCTION, not by discipline — the single best structural fact in this neighbourhood. vite.config.ts:23-41 GENERATES the demo's self-alias set from `package.json#exports` ('GENERATED (not hand-rolled) so the alias set can never drift from the exports map'), so a specifier a real consumer could not write cannot resolve. `safeAccentColor`'s dual-ratio certification (src/color/operations.ts:228-236) is genuinely rigorous and is the reason the F-3 chain can be trusted at all: it takes `Math.min(floatRatio, byteRatio)` — the unclipped-luminance ratio AND the 8-bit-rendered ratio — so it will never certify an ink that the actual painted pixels would fail. Its `contrast_unreachable` refusal (:257-259) is CORRECT behaviour; the demo's `?? ""` is what turns a correct refusal into a lie. The library is more honest than its consumer.

`demo/color-session/ink.ts:1-11` composes the library instead of re-implementing it — `convertColor`, `mixColors`, `oklch`, `safeAccentColor`, `parseCssColor`, `serializeCssColor` in, and only POLICY out. Given this repo's history (the gl-matrix extirpation, the S.W2-2 'the demo carries NO norm/denorm color math' clause quoted at useContrastSafeColor.ts:33-36), holding that line across a 4,000-file demo is a real achievement.

Same file, `ChannelMeta` (:40-46) and the `unit`/`percent`/`hue` constructors (:48-50) are a small, exact, readable schema vocabulary.

The powerless-hue hazard is UNDERSTOOD and documented where it is handled — useColorParsing.ts:39-46 wraps the HSV hue read in try/catch with the comment 'Powerless colors have no numeric hue; retain the last deliberate hue.', useColorPipeline.ts:86-94 repeats the guard with an `s*v > 0.01` predicate, ComponentSliders.vue:128-130 guards the alpha sentinel, and `HSVCurrentColor` (useColorPipeline.ts:105-108) deliberately re-injects `stableHue` so a powerless hue can never reach the spectrum.
