The binding motion sweep measured it: both guards fire (animation-duration 1e-05s) and are structurally powerless against a timeline-driven animation, with .pane-header-title reading transform: matrix(0.805831,…) and height 43.98 → 35.44 px at scrollTop 200 identically in both modes. Blast radius named there as nine panes. Against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6: "Reduced motion resolves directly to the final geometry and stable chromatic state." Note this row also OVER-turns pass 4's own narrowing — see the KILLED list.

confirmed.claim: "Find by Color" is a silent partial search: an undocumented magic radius, a client-side filter over only the loaded page, and a silent return-false for any palette without an index.
confirmed.proof: BrowsePane.vue:336-355 is fully static: colorSearchParams is pane-local (:336); displayedBrowse (:339-349) filters pm.filteredBrowse with `const radius = 0.15` (:343) and `if (!oklabColors || oklabColors.length === 0) return false;` (:346); the comment at :353-354 declines the server predicate the client already types and serializes (demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius, zero callers repo-wide). Consequences follow structurally: the pager at :133 keys pm.hasMore, which the pane-local filter cannot see, so it offers more of a wall the filter has already emptied; and a zero-match colour search lands in the false empty plate (:85). Live corroboration is strong and independent: 5 of 10 rows on the production commons carry oklabColors: [] (pass 3 D3-06, pass 4 N-13, CHALLENGE-C P-4), so half the shipped commons is unreachable by colour search for every colour, forever. One narrowing I record rather than a kill: 0.15 is not arbitrary — it is the server's own documented default (crud-list.ts query.colorRadius ?? 0.15), so the defect is a *duplicated protocol constant with two editable homes*, which is sharper than "a bare literal"; and pass 1's "admits most of colour space" overstates a ~0.014-unit ball in a gamut whose ball would mostly fall outside it.

confirmed.claim: Changing the sort has no visible state anywhere; the filter register never counts sort or the text query.
confirmed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:189-195 verbatim: `const activeFilterCount = computed(() => { let count = 0; if (tier) count++; count += selectedTags.length; if (colorSearchActive.value) count++; return count; })`. Sort is absent; the text query is absent. The whole refinement grammar lives behind one 32px EllipsisVertical trigger at :5, whose only register is the badge at :7-12 gated on activeFilterCount > 0. So switching Newest → Most Popular → Most Forked changes the badge by zero, changes no label, and silently reorders the wall. Against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 ("Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value … are explicit") and PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07.

confirmed.claim: The specimen strip draws N adjacent colour cells with no separator between them and no edge against the card body, so perceptually adjacent palette members render as one undivided block.
confirmed.proof: Static: PaletteColorStrip.vue:13-23 renders each segment as a bare <div class="shrink-0"> with only backgroundColor and a width/height percentage — no border, no gap (the parent at :6-11 is a plain flex with no gap), no divider, and no outer rule where the strip meets the card body. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 requires that "boundaries … meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier". The strip therefore has no boundary to meet any contrast on, in either scheme, for any palette. The two seats' *numbers* disagree on method (pass 1 R2.2 used WCAG CR 1.41:1; pass 2 D-23 correctly re-measured in OKLab, ΔE 0.0878 cell↔cell and 0.0998 cell↔stage against a neutral-ramp step of 0.064–0.110) and I cannot re-derive either without a browser — but the design gap they are both measuring is structural and needs no probe: a five-step neutral ramp, the single most common artifact a colour tool produces, has nothing drawn between its steps.

confirmed.claim: The pane's scroll host is named .pane-scroll-fade, implements no fade, hides its scrollbar, and terminates by slicing a colour specimen through the middle.
confirmed.proof: demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:54-57 is the entire definition: `.pane-scroll-fade { contain: layout style paint; scroll-timeline: --pane-scroll block; }`. Two properties. No mask-image, no gradient, no ::after fade. BrowsePane.vue:2 applies it together with overflow-y-auto h-full. Independently re-measured by a fourth, non-D seat: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md M-33 (probe3 on a live mounted pane) reads mask-image: none, -webkit-mask-image: none, ::before background-image: none, ::after = the paper-grain data-URI, and rules the "bottom fade" claim FALSE — i.e. the fade does not exist. A class whose name asserts an affordance it does not deliver is legacy naming (owner edict 2); it is also the reason the terminus reads as a paint fault rather than a scroll boundary.

confirmed.claim: The search field's visible chrome is larger than its operable target: the bar root is a <div>, not a <label>, so the field's padding is dead to the pointer.
confirmed.proof: Static from the producer bytes: glass-ui 7.0.0's SearchBar renders its root as <component :is="tag"> with props tag: { default: "div" } (SearchBar.vue.d.ts:4-12 and dist/search.js), applies class "input-bar" to it, and mounts the <input class="input-bar-field"> as a child with no wrapping <label>, no for/id pairing and no @click on the root. So clicking anywhere on the bar that is not the input itself focuses nothing. BrowsePane.vue:10 consumes the default tag. PROPORTION-AUDIT §5.7 ("Visual glyph size, operable target size and layout reservation are separate quantities") is the owning row. The specific 5.7 px dead bands and the 36 px/24.6 px pair are a single-seat live read I could not reproduce — the structural defect does not depend on them.

confirmed.claim: Four computed type sizes sit in one items-center metadata row so nothing shares a baseline, and one of the four is unauthored.
confirmed.proof: Citations are exact against live bytes. PaletteCard.vue:43 opens the row with flex items-center; the identity span at :55 is font-display font-medium text-subheading; PaletteCardMeta.vue:53 is text-mono-small; the fork/version/tag chips at :9, :18, :28, :39 are text-micro; and the vote <button> at :43-45 carries a long utility string with NO type class at all, so its font-size is inherited and its child <span> then resets to text-mono-small. Three rungs were chosen; the fourth is a leak. Against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:66-77's closed type matrix, which assigns one role per rung.

confirmed.claim: BrowsePane names one object four different ways across seven authored strings, and the header — the first line a visitor reads — is the one that does not say "commons".
confirmed.proof: All seven line citations are byte-exact against the live file: :3 description="Discover palettes from the community."; :13 placeholder="Search the commons..."; :65 message="The commons is unreachable."; :84 empty-eyebrow="· the commons ·"; :85 empty-text="No published palettes here yet."; :86 empty-hint="Publish one from My Palettes and start the wall."; :142 "More from the commons". "The wall" appears in exactly one user-visible string while being the term the source comments use throughout (:29, :41, :121) — internal vocabulary leaking into copy at one site. The empty plate's instruction asks the user to act on the one noun that appears nowhere else in the UI.

confirmed.claim: cardRefs is a write-only registry that never releases an entry, so verdicts for save/delete/visibility/fork can be delivered into a detached component.
confirmed.proof: BrowsePane.vue:94 — :ref="(el: any) => el && (cardRefs[palette.slug] = el)" — and :209 — reactive<Record<string, InstanceType<typeof PaletteCard>>>({}). Vue invokes a function ref with null on unmount (@vue/runtime-core setRef: `const value = isUnmount ? null : refValue`), and the `el &&` guard short-circuits exactly that call, so no key is ever deleted. Consumers at :228-230, :237-241, :249 and :264 route every operation verdict through that map, and PaletteCard's only feedback channel is the imperative defineExpose({ showFeedback }) at PaletteCard.vue:244. Design consequence, which is the part my lens owns: the pane replaces its row set wholesale on every sort/tier/tag/search change, so a verdict that arrives after a re-render is written into a component that is not in the document and the user is told nothing — and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 forbids exactly that ("A transient flourish may celebrate success but never carries the only truth").

killed.id: challenge-D-design-pass2.md:656 — the KILL of pass-1 R2.6
killed.claim: "R2.6 the route's primary control has no accessible name → KILLED. SearchFilterBar.vue:5 — aria-label=\"Filters\". REPORT.md records namelessButtons for /#/browse = 0 in all four matrices, and my Tab walk reads the name."
killed.refutation: Category error: pass 2 refuted a claim about an <input> with evidence about a <button>. R2.6's own probe output names its subject explicitly — `"nameless": ["INPUT.input-bar-field rect=373x24.87"]` — and R2.6 itself points out that the namelessButtons metric counts only <button>, which is precisely the metric pass 2 then cites as the refutation. Live bytes settle it: glass-ui 7.0.0's SearchBar renders <input type="search" … class="input-bar-field"> with no aria-label, no id, no <label>, no aria-labelledby (dist/search.js, SearchBar setup), its prop list has no ariaLabel (dist/components/search/SearchBar.vue.d.ts:4-12), and BrowsePane.vue:10-14 passes only v-model, class and placeholder. SearchFilterBar.vue:5 does carry aria-label="Filters" — for the trigger button, a different element. R2.6 stands and is restored to CONFIRMED.

killed.id: challenge-D-design-pass3.md:85-133 — D3-01's mechanism and its prescribed cure
killed.claim: "The mobile search field clips its own placeholder mid-word … a permanent, post-fonts.ready, two-engine geometry defect that appears only on the real mobile control rung — the arm pass 2 did not measure. 21px type in a 217px box." Cure: "SearchBar gains a producer `label` affordance … Until then, ::placeholder { text-overflow: ellipsis } at the producer root."
killed.refutation: Two limbs, both refuted against live bytes. (a) THERE IS NO MOBILE CONTROL RUNG. `grep -rn coarse demo/` returns four sites — GradientStopEditor, ConfigSliderPane, ComponentSliders, and a comment — none of which touches the search field; glass-ui 7.0.0's shipped CSS contains one `coarse` occurrence, also unrelated; no `text-size-adjust` declaration exists anywhere in demo/ or the producer; and no width media query alters the field's type. A uniform 1.5× inflation of BOTH font-size (14 → 21) and bar height (36 → 54) while the layout measure is essentially unchanged (236 → 217) is the signature of engine text-autosizing under Playwright's device descriptor (isMobile + deviceScaleFactor 3), not an authored rung — a CSS rung would have to exist somewhere and it does not. Pass 2's KILL was right about the authored geometry and wrong about the cause; pass 3's overturn is right about the capture and wrong about the mechanism. (b) THE PRESCRIBED PRODUCER ASK IS UNNECESSARY. glass-ui's SearchBar is `inheritAttrs: false` and computes `o = computed(() => { const { class: _, ...t } = attrs; return t })`, then spreads `o.value` ONTO THE INPUT (`b("input", w({ ref, type: "search" }, o.value, { value, placeholder, class: "input-bar-field", onInput }))`). So `<SearchBar aria-label="Search the commons">` lands on the input today, with zero producer change and no ASK-D dependency. What survives, and is worth carrying: `text-overflow` is never set on `.input-bar-field`, so any overflow severs mid-word with no ellipsis; and the placeholder is load-bearing only because the field has no name (R2.6). The rendered clip in the audit's own iPhone-14 captures is real; its attribution to a design rung is not.

killed.claim: "filtering ten results to zero, a sort completing, a page arriving, and a load failing all announce nothing" / "no status region exists: filtering 10 results to 0 announces nothing. liveRegions: 0 in both engines."
killed.refutation: The filtered-to-zero limb is false, and the corpus refutes itself. demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:28 gives the empty branch role="status" — an implicit aria-live="polite" region — and that is exactly the element BrowsePane renders when displayedBrowse.length === 0 (via PaletteCardGrid.vue:24-31). Pass 3's own D3-07 measured `statusRole: true` in the identical filtered-to-zero reproduction. The `liveRegions: 0` figure comes from counting [aria-live] ATTRIBUTES, which role=status never carries. The correct, narrower statement — which nobody in the corpus wrote — is that Browse has NO PERSISTENT status region: it has a transient one in three of its four states (4× role=status skeletons while loading, role=status when empty, role=alert on error) and NONE in the populated state. So emptiness announces (falsely, per D-06) while arrivals — 50 cards landing, a page appending, a sort completing — are the states that are genuinely silent. That inversion is the finding; "announces nothing" is not.

killed.claim: "the two loading states carry no accessible name … The label is dropped. Confirmed by construction and consistent with the measured aria-busy: 0 / aria-live: [] — the loading states are inaudible."
killed.refutation: The premise is right and the consequence is inverted. The wrapper <div aria-label> at BrowsePane.vue:47 and :128 does map to role=generic and its name is prohibited — that half stands. But its CHILDREN are named live regions: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:35-36 gives every skeleton root role="status" aria-label="Loading palette", and BrowsePane mounts SKELETON_COUNT = 4 of them (:49-53) plus 2 more for paging (:130). The loading state is therefore OVER-announced — four simultaneous identical polite regions on entry, two more on every page turn — not inaudible. CHALLENGE-C pass 2 (N-5, N-6) reached this and corrected its own pass 1; the D axis carried the "inaudible" framing forward through five passes without noticing. Citation drift also recorded: the C axis cites PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:44-47; the live coordinates are :35-36.

killed.claim: "what it renders is not a slug line: the live subtree reports { t: \"button\", … al: \"Copy slug user-1\" } — a named action button, not provenance text." / "A slug is provenance; rendering it as a clipboard action … is neither."
killed.refutation: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardSwatches.vue:3-11, under the comment ``, renders `{{ displaySlug }}` — the slug IS shown, as text, on exactly the `text-mono-small` rung VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:75 assigns to "value, code, or provenance". The `Copy slug` control at :13-19 is its labelled SIBLING, with aria-hidden on the icon and a proper accessible name. The seat's probe walked to the focusable element, found the button, and concluded the text did not exist. D4-03's FIRST limb stands untouched — the whole block is gated behind `v-if="expanded"` (PaletteCard.vue:140) so `show-slug` is inert on the collapsed wall — and a sharper defect is hiding underneath it; see the MISSED list.

killed.id: challenge-D-design-pass2.md:655 — the KILL of pass-1 R2.8
killed.claim: "R2.8 `.pane-scroll-fade` promises a fade the CSS never implements → KILLED. PaneHeader.vue:54–57 defines scroll-timeline: --pane-scroll block; the header's ::before veil (:63–80) is its consumer. The fade exists; the producer/consumer pair is simply split across one file boundary."
killed.refutation: The cited lines are the refutation. demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:54-57 declares exactly two properties — `contain: layout style paint` and `scroll-timeline: --pane-scroll block` — and neither is a fade. The ::before veil pass 2 points at is a TOP-edge material on `.pane-header`, a different element from the pane root that carries `.pane-scroll-fade`; it cannot be "the consumer" of a bottom-terminus affordance the class name asserts. Independently settled by a fourth, non-D seat with a live probe: codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md M-33 rules the existence of a bottom fade FALSE — mask-image: none, -webkit-mask-image: none, ::before background-image: none, ::after = the paper-grain data-URI — and names the class "a misnomer surviving a retired mechanism". Pass 3's D3-04 re-raise is correct; pass 2's KILL is withdrawn.

killed.claim: "Pass 2's proof holds for the transform arm and fails for the opacity arm. That argument is defensible for `pane-title-shrink`, a pure transform: scale() whose from-state equals the base state. The correct verb is TIGHTEN on `pane-desc-shrink`, not a wholesale PRM gate."
killed.refutation: The transform arm is not defensible, and the binding motion sweep measured it. codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md MQ-1, probe3 at scrollTop 200 on a live pane: `.pane-header-title` reads `transform: matrix(0.805831, 0, 0, 0.805831, 0, 0)` and height 43.98 → 35.44 px BYTE-IDENTICALLY at `no-preference` and at `reduce` — a ~19 % spatial scale, scrubbed by scroll position, running for a user who asked for reduced motion. "From-state equals base state" is irrelevant: the user does not sit at scroll 0, and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6 requires reduced motion to "resolve directly to the final geometry", not to scrub toward it. D4-06's finding is therefore CONFIRMED and UNDER-CLAIMED: the cure is `animation-timeline: none` (or `animation: none`) on all three selectors inside a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block in PaneHeader.vue, not a TIGHTEN on the opacity arm alone.

missed.claim: In the state the wall reaches most often — emptied by typed text alone — ALL FOUR recovery affordances are simultaneously absent, and the absence is produced by one predicate. `activeFilterCount` (SearchFilterBar.vue:189-195) counts tier + tags + colour and NOT the text query; the filter-count badge is gated on it (`v-if="activeFilterCount > 0"`, :8) AND SO IS THE ENTIRE "Clear all filters" CONTROL (`<div v-if="activeFilterCount > 0" class="px-3 py-2">`, :110-120). So on a text-only filter there is (1) no badge, (2) no clear-filters control anywhere in the product, (3) no action on the plate (the #emptyAction slot is unused, D5-04), and (4) copy that says the commons is empty and tells you to go publish (D-06). The only exit is for the user to guess that the text they typed is the cause, re-select it and delete it.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:189-195 (the computed, text query absent), :7-12 (the badge, gated), :110-120 (the Clear-all Button, gated on the identical predicate); demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:80-91 (no #emptyAction, hard-coded strings). Pass 1's D-06 quotes the computed and even cites the clear control's line range ("buried inside the ⋮ popover, SearchFilterBar.vue:110–119") but concludes only that it is *buried* — it is not buried in this state, it is not rendered. Pass 5's D5-04 owns the missing plate action but does not join it to the badge predicate. No pass in six D passes states that one `v-if` deletes two of the four exits at once. CHALLENGE-C P-2 makes this the dominant case rather than a corner: typing the second character of any word empties the commons (measured `o`→3 cards, `oc`→0, `ocean`→1 against the live production wall), so this dead end is reached on nearly every real query.

missed.claim: The vote control is a toggle whose only state register is a hard-coded Tailwind palette colour, with no `aria-pressed` and no state in its accessible name — the exact construction VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 forbids by name, on the one control the corpus itself establishes is the card's de-facto accessible representative.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardMeta.vue:43-54: a bare <button> with :aria-label="`${palette.voteCount ?? 0} votes, click to vote`" (:46) — the name encodes the count and an imperative but never whether the user has voted — and the Heart at :49-52 expresses the entire voted/not-voted state as `:class="palette.voted ? 'fill-red-500 text-red-500' : 'text-muted-foreground'"`. No aria-pressed, no role=switch, no text change. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.1: "Selected, failed, pending, withdrawn and disabled states are never color-only. Role, accessible name, state/value and associated error/status are explicit." Second limb, same two lines: `fill-red-500`/`text-red-500` are raw Tailwind palette literals in a design-token codebase — a repo-wide census of `(text|bg|fill|border|stroke)-(red|blue|green|…)-\d{2,3}` over demo/ returns nine sites total, two of which are these, while the sibling atom EmptyState.vue:19 correctly uses `text-destructive/80`. On a colour tool, the one state mark on the commons wall is an un-tokened swatch. Pass 4's D4-05 raised the *name's* grammar ("1 votes") and its mis-scoping; nobody raised the missing pressed state or the token breach.

missed.claim: The card's provenance chip silently shows two different kinds of identifier in identical chrome depending on data, so on the public commons half the wall is attributed to an author and half is labelled with the palette's own slug — with the markup, the accessible name and the copy action all calling both "slug".
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:231 — `const displaySlug = computed(() => props.palette.userSlug ?? props.palette.slug)`. It is passed at :143 and rendered at PaletteCardSwatches.vue:8-11 in a single pill under the comment `<!-- User slug display -->` (:3), with the copy button's name built as `Copy slug ${displaySlug}` (:15). CHALLENGE-L pass 4 (N-11) measured the live production commons: 5 of 10 rows carry `userSlug: null`, so exactly half the wall silently falls through to the palette slug. Same chrome, same label, same aria pattern, two different objects — and the one place attribution matters is a public wall. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7 ("Principal attribution renders only the supplied principal identity") is the owning line, quoted in the corpus by pass 4's D4-03 in support of a different, refuted claim. The correct design move is to render nothing when there is no principal, not to substitute a different object's identifier.

missed.claim: BrowsePane applies the Fraunces display family to two of its three controls, breaching VISUAL-CONSTITUTION's closed type matrix at the pane's OWN authored coordinates — a violation the corpus found in a shared atom and never checked in the file under audit.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:72 (`class="font-display"` on the Retry <Button>, :69-76) and :139 (`class="font-display"` on the "More from the commons" <Button>, :136-143). VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:74 assigns "control or label, including dropdown options" to `text-small` / **Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold**; :78 declares the matrix "closed across all eighteen compositions", and Fraunces owns only text-display, --type-title and --type-subheading (:70-72). Pass 2's D-25 found the same law broken inside EmptyState.vue:20/:58 (`font-display text-heading`) and filed it as an eight-consumer atom defect — correctly — but no pass in six checked BrowsePane's own two `font-display` sites, which are the only two type decisions the pane authors for itself.

missed.claim: Three of the card's four metadata marks carry their entire meaning in a `title` attribute — hover-only, unavailable on touch, unreliable in AT — and two of them are the SAME glyph with two different meanings, 30 px apart in one row.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCardMeta.vue: the fork *indicator* at :7-13 is a <span> whose only content is a `GitFork` icon with meaning carried by `:title="`Remixed from ${palette.forkOf}`"` (:10) — no text, no accessible name on a non-interactive span, so it is invisible to touch and to AT entirely; the fork *count* at :16-23 uses the IDENTICAL `GitFork` glyph (:21) with `:title="`${palette.forkCount} remix…`"` (:19); the version count at :26-33 is `:title="`${palette.versionCount} versions`"` (:29). PROPORTION-AUDIT PR-07 ("Hover-only/unlabeled controls and invisible … state → ADD-AFFORDANCE", quoted by pass 2's D-18 for a different control) and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5 law 5 ("A small icon/mark is either data, status, labeled action, drag affordance, focus/selection register or removed") are both the owning rows. Pass 1's R2.7 gestured at the cluster's flat weighting; nobody named the duplicate glyph or the title-only meanings.

missed.claim: BrowsePane's own template has an unreachable style intent: the pane Card carries `w-full mx-auto` together, where `mx-auto` can never take effect, alongside `pane-scroll-fade` whose `contain: paint` makes the pane root a second paint clip stacked above the grid's.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:2 — `class="pane-scroll-fade w-full mx-auto overflow-y-auto overflow-x-hidden min-w-0 h-full"`. `mx-auto` centres a box narrower than its container; `w-full` guarantees it is not. Separately, `.pane-scroll-fade` resolves to `contain: layout style paint` (PaneHeader.vue:54-57), so the pane root is itself a paint-clipping box wrapping the grid's `contain: content` (PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52) — two nested paint clips around a register (`cartoon-surface`) whose entire grammar is paint that escapes its border box. Pass 5's D5-03 found the inner clip and attributed the whole defect to it; the pane root's clip is a second, independent one that the same cure must account for. Filed MINOR because the dead utility is cosmetic and the outer clip has gutters (px-4 sm:px-6) where the inner one has none.

unproven: D3-02 (pass 3) — the filter trigger measured at 32 × 40 px, `border-radius: 9999px` at aspect 0.8, overhanging a 36 px bar by 2 px top and bottom. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE and its attribution is not locatable: the report blames "the producer's min-height: 40px" beating the consumer's `h-8`, but glass-ui 7.0.0 ships no `.button` rule at all in dist/glass-ui.css or dist/styles/**, and the only `min-height: var(--control-h-md)` in the producer is on `.tags-input`. The consumer class `relative h-8 w-8` at SearchFilterBar.vue:5 is confirmed; the computed geometry and its cause are a single-seat live read I cannot reproduce under probe parsimony.

D3-01's symptom (pass 3) — whether a real iPhone reproduces the severed placeholder. The clip IS present in the audit's own WebKit captures (shots/safari-mobile-light/browse.png, shots/rtl-mobile/browse.png) and those were taken through devices["iPhone 14"], so the emulation path is consistent; but with the mechanism refuted (see KILLED), the question of whether real-device text-autosizing produces it is undecided without hardware.

D-23 / R2.2 — the numeric dark-scheme specimen contrast (WCAG 1.41:1 vs OKLab ΔE 0.0878/0.0998). Two seats, two metrics, one correcting the other; both are pixel samples from captures I cannot re-take. The STRUCTURAL half — no separator, no gap, no edge between strip cells or against the card body — is confirmed statically and filed above.

D-08 (pass 1) — a failed sort shipping a stale wall under the new sort's label. The branch shape is verified statically (useBrowsePalettes.ts:117-119 sets sortMode before awaiting; the catch at :77-82 sets browseError but never clears remotePalettes; BrowsePane.vue:62 requires displayedBrowse.length === 0 so the error branch is suppressed on a populated wall). The report labels the runtime arm a code-proven hypothesis and it remains one — it needs a reachable API that then fails a sort request.

D-21 (pass 2) — the 471.7 px layout collapse on route re-entry. Mechanism is structurally sound (usePaletteWiring's unguarded browse watcher re-requests on every entry; SKELETON_COUNT = 4 at BrowsePane.vue:207 can never equal the row count), but the measured collapse is single-seat and single-engine.

D-01/D-16/P-1's permanence limb specifically — that the blank survives a backend restore and a route round-trip (CHALLENGE-C P-1's six-step recovery table). The blank itself is three-seat/two-engine; the unrecoverability matrix is one seat.
superlatives: demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue is the best-designed atom in this component's graph, and the pane's failure is that it under-uses it. Two species are separated at the ROLE level, not by copy — role="alert" for error (:17) and role="status" for empty (:28) — with the rule written into the file header (:2-13, "loading ≠ empty, error ≠ empty"). It carries reading measures (max-w-[26ch] / [44ch] / [36ch]), a threaded #action slot (:26, :64), and a caption ink rung that records its own contrast measurement and why the previous token failed (:49-54 and :95-101: `--muted-foreground` "composited 3.84:1 over the My Palettes plate in light (< the 4.5:1 small-text floor)"). Eight consumers inherit the cure. D5-04's finding is precisely that BrowsePane declines the affordance this atom already offers it.

PaletteColorStrip's weighted-segment design (PaletteColorStrip.vue:47-71). The specimen sizes proportionally to the quantizer's population story carried on the palette itself, with `WEIGHT_FLOOR = 0.08` so small clusters stay legible, renormalising after the floor is applied, and falling back cleanly to equal widths when no weights exist. The rationale is written at :38-44. That is a real, thought-through specimen decision — the strip tells you not just which colours but how much of each — and it is the reason D5-01's forced-colors omission is worth a BLOCKER rather than a shrug.

foundation.css's two-tier forced-colors + print policy built around ONE named colour-surface roster (:653-696 and :793-841), with the reasoning stated in the source: a blanket WHCM substitution "would DESTROY the color content the tool exists to show", so tier 1 keeps colour on the display surfaces and tier 2 lets the chrome adopt system colours, plus a restored `outline` because box-shadow focus rings vanish in WHCM. Most codebases never make this decision at all. It is also why D5-01's cure is one roster line instead of a redesign — pass 5 got this exactly right in framing the defect as failed enrolment rather than absence.

PaletteCardSkeleton's motion discipline (PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:2-31, :103-123). Two temporal registers with stated semantics — `shadow` for a known-imminent local wait, `developing` for an unknown-duration network wait — and the announcement contract split from the motion contract in one sentence: "loading ≠ empty now splits on ANNOUNCEMENT, not motion: this shell keeps role=\"status\" + \"Loading palette\" because HERE work IS happening; the aria-hidden ghost announces nothing." The stagger is written through the producer's published seams (`--skeleton-shimmer-delay`, `--skeleton-shimmer-tint`) with an explicit refusal to fork the producer keyframes, and the breath is tuned only through `--pulse-aura-opacity-max` / `--animate-ambient-pulse-easing`. Consuming a producer seam that is not yet live, rather than re-implementing it, is the right call and it is documented as such.

The app-wide motion architecture, and BrowsePane's conformance to it. BrowsePane defines zero local keyframes, deletes none, and names only producer tokens: `<Transition name="vj-morph">` (:40) keys one of the three sanctioned families defined centrally in demo/styles/animations.css, and `duration-fast` (:88) resolves to a real 0.2s. The binding motion sweep independently found 21 prefers-reduced-motion rules in the served CSSOM, two global neutralisers whose interaction is stronger than either alone (the property-list rewrite deletes transform/max-height/border-radius/filter from every transition rather than merely shortening them), a `[data-allow-motion]` opt-in that still cannot produce an infinite animation under reduce, and a deliberately source-ordered overlay carve-out. Five D passes each independently attacked the motion axis and each independently failed to break it.

PaletteCard.vue:228-230 — `const { safeCss } = useSafeAccentFn("well")`, with the comment "the card IS the rung-2 WELL (Q4) — ink certifies on THAT tier." The card certifies its ink against the actual material it sits on rather than trusting a token name, which is verbatim what VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §4.1 demands ("Text, focus, boundaries and state meet their rendered contrast on the actual material tier; a token name is not evidence"). The same discipline appears in EmptyState's `.plate-ink` rung. Wherever this codebase actually applied its own contrast law it applied it correctly; the defects are where the law was never reached, not where it was reached and ignored.

CHALLENGE-C pass 3's probe method (probe-c3-live-proxy.mjs) deserves its own row: a 20-line Node re-issuing proxy that fulfils the page with the REAL production bytes, defeating both the localhost misconfig latch and the API's CORS allow-list that had forced every prior seat in this programme to stub the wall. killed.claim: "The latch — designed to stop doomed requests — is what makes the retry fail fast enough to deadlock the transition. The faster the failure, the more certain the blank"; `out-in` "holds isLeaving and the pending child never mounts."
killed.refutation: REFUTED against Vue 3.5.35's actual source. `mode="out-in"` has an explicit recovery path: node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:1413-1420 installs `leavingHooks.afterLeave = () => { state.isLeaving = false; instance.update(); … }`, and :6676-6681's `performRemove` invokes it after `hostRemove`. `instance.update` is an unconditional `effect.run.bind(effect)` (:6190), so a second same-microtask flip does NOT strand anything — the transition re-renders the current branch the moment the leave completes. Speed of failure is irrelevant. The real mechanism is a template shape nobody looked at: demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:2-13 opens with a template comment, so in DEV the SFC compiles to a multi-root fragment with patchFlag 2112 (2048 DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT | 64) — verified by compiling the SFC offline with @vue/compiler-sfc 3.5.35 (`hasFragmentRoot: true`). `setTransitionHooks` (runtime-core.cjs.js) stops at that fragment and never reaches its children, so `remove()`'s DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT branch at :6656-6670 recurses into a child with NO `transition` — neither the leave animation nor `transition.afterLeave()` runs, and `state.isLeaving` is never reset. This also predicts the data better: it explains why `skeletons: 0` in every frame and why the plate vanishes instantly on click rather than after a leave.

killed.claim: "Pressing `Retry` on the error plate permanently destroys the Browse wall" — filed BLOCKER on the basis that this is what production users see.
killed.refutation: NOT ESTABLISHED FOR THE SHIPPED BUILD. Every probe in the corpus drives a dev server (challenge-C-implementation.md:46-48 `http://192.168.1.166:9000`; challenge-D-design.md:81 `http://localhost:9000`). The defect is gated on the DEV compiler: `@vue/compiler-core`'s parser default is `comments: true` in node_modules/@vue/compiler-core/dist/compiler-core.cjs.js:2308 and `comments: false` in dist/compiler-core.cjs.prod.js, and DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT (2048) does not appear anywhere in the prod compiler bundle (`grep -c 2048` → 0). Under `vite build` (NODE_ENV=production) demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue therefore compiles single-root — I verified this directly, compiling the same SFC with `isProd: true` gives `hasFragmentRoot: false` — so `remove()` takes the element path, the leave runs, `afterLeave` fires, `state.isLeaving` resets and the error plate re-mounts. In production the symptom degrades to a ~1-transition blank, not a permanent one. The BLOCKER as written ("the most-photographed state of this route … silently and permanently destroys the surface") is a dev-server claim presented as a shipped-product claim.

killed.claim: Cure 3: "`Retry` must not re-enter the *initial-load* state … A retry is a refresh, not a first load — the same distinction the sort path already makes with `isSort`."
killed.refutation: UNSOUND as a standalone cure. With `loadRemotePalettes(true)` the retry sets `sortLoading` instead of `browsing` (demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:63-69) so the branch does not flip on FAILURE — but on SUCCESS `browseError` goes null and `displayedBrowse` becomes non-empty, so BrowsePane.vue:62 → :81 still flips `error` → `wall`, the EmptyState still leaves, and the same strand occurs. Cure 3 converts "blank on retry-failure" into "blank on retry-success". Cures 1 and 2 do hold; the cheapest correct cure — moving the leading comment inside demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue's root element — is absent from all three axes.

killed.claim: "The shim converts a benign warning into a hard render failure on a strictly wider input set" / "Without the coercion … The pane renders."
killed.refutation: The argument switches inputs mid-comparison and the conclusion does not follow. The "without" branch is evaluated on an OBJECT payload (`undefined > 0` → false → section hides); the "with" branch is evaluated on `null`/`undefined`. On the actual null/undefined input the un-coerced path ALSO throws: demo/palettes/browser/search/SearchFilterBar.vue:47 is `v-if="availableTags.length > 0"` on a destructured required prop, so `undefined.length` is a TypeError in SearchFilterBar's render, not a benign warning. And on the object input the coercion is strictly SAFER — `Object.values(obj)` renders the tags where the un-coerced path silently hides the whole Tags section. So the coercion is differently-unsafe on one two-element input set, never "strictly less safe on a strictly wider" one. The recommendation (delete demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:210-220 as dead defensive code, per pass 2 N-7) still stands on its own; the severity argument does not.

killed.claim: "The server at least pages honestly across a colour filter … the client copy cannot" — implying that threading `colorL/colorA/colorB/colorRadius` into `currentFilterOpts()` cures the 5-of-10 blindness.
killed.refutation: Half-refuted. The paging limb is true, but the blindness limb is identical on the server: api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:159-181's `colorMatcherFor` contains the same `const oklabColors = p.oklabColors; if (!oklabColors || oklabColors.length === 0) return false;`. Moving the predicate server-side changes nothing about which rows can match. (P-4's own parenthetical concedes the producer-side `computeOklabColors` gap, but the cure sentence reads as if the move fixes it.) Worth recording alongside: the client plumbing for that cure already exists and is dead — demo/palettes/api/palettes.ts:27-30 and :50-53 declare and serialise all four colour params and have zero callers in demo/.

killed.claim: "the seam's docstring asserts the opposite of what the graph shows — that external consumers come through the top, when in fact 3 of the 4 external consumers come through the side."
killed.refutation: FALSE as quoted. demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:5-6 reads "External consumers reach the feature through THIS seam **(or a sub-barrel it re-exports)**, never a raw internal `.vue` file" — the parenthetical the finding drops is exactly the sanction for side reach. And :9-16 goes further, documenting the side path as the intended one: "App.vue's eager `index.js` chunk therefore still reaches `MigratePalettesDialog` through the `dialog/` sub-barrel directly … the seam's presence is the public contract; the sub-barrel is the tree-shake-honest reach." Every one of the cited external imports is a sub-barrel import (`…/palettes/browser/card`), i.e. exactly what the docstring authorises. The seam is over-declared, not lying; the finding's real content is the card cluster's home, which survives.

killed.claim: "`defineExpose` on `PaletteCard.vue:244` is part of a contract three workbenches also consume."
killed.refutation: FALSE by enumeration. `grep -rn showFeedback demo/` returns exactly two consumers of the exposed method, both inside demo/palettes: demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:230, :239, :249, :264 and demo/palettes/PalettesPane.vue:207. Neither demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue nor demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue nor demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractWorkbench.vue takes a template ref on PaletteCard or touches its exposed surface — they consume props and events only. The cross-feature coupling the finding needs is real for the props/events contract and does not extend to the imperative one.

killed.claim: "`trigger: 1` throughout. The button never disappears from the document, so this is *not* the 'affordance unmounts' story … it means adding a `:disabled` state to the button would not fix it" and "`loadingBlock: 0` at every frame … the designed loading state … **never rendered once**."
killed.refutation: Both limbs are contradicted by the template. demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:125-144 is a `v-if="pm.loadingMore.value"` / `v-else-if="pm.hasMore.value && …"` pair — mutually exclusive branches. `loadMoreRemotePalettes` sets `loadingMore.value = true` synchronously (demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:101) before awaiting, so the focused trigger IS unmounted on the very next flush; that is precisely the "affordance unmounts" story, and keeping a mounted node (the `:disabled` shape) is therefore a live candidate cure rather than a proven dead end. The "never rendered once" claim rests on six discrete samples beginning at t+30ms (challenge-D-design.md:228-235); a branch that mounts and unmounts inside 30ms is invisible to that sampling, so absence of the skeleton in the samples is not evidence of absence in the frame sequence. The symptom the finding is actually about — focus BUTTON→BODY with nothing announced, and `statusRegions: 1` belonging to the other pane — survives intact.

missed.claim: The leading template comment in `EmptyState.vue` makes it a multi-root component under the dev compiler, which breaks every `<Transition>` that has to lift it out — the true root cause of P-1, and a one-line cure no seat proposed. `PaletteCard.vue` and `PaletteCardSkeleton.vue` are the same shape and are latent hazards for any future `<Transition>` over them.
missed.proof: demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:2-13 opens the `<template>` with an HTML comment before the `v-if`/`v-else` pair. Compiled offline with @vue/compiler-sfc 3.5.35: dev → `return (_openBlock(), _createElementBlock(_Fragment, null, [ _createCommentVNode(…), …], 2112 /* STABLE_FRAGMENT, DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT */))`; prod → single-root `_createElementBlock("div", …)`. The same compile over demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue and demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardSkeleton.vue also yields 2112 (PaletteCardGrid.vue does not). Consequence chain in node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js: `setTransitionHooks` assigns `transition` to the component vnode and its subTree (the fragment) and stops; `remove()` at :6656-6670 takes the `patchFlag & 2048` branch and recurses into children that carry no `transition`, so `performRemove`'s `transition.afterLeave()` at :6676-6681 never fires; `afterLeave` is the sole reset for `state.isLeaving` (:1413-1420), and the BaseTransition render short-circuits on it. Cure: move the comment inside the root element (or give EmptyState a single wrapper root). That is strictly cheaper and strictly more general than any of P-1's three prescribed cures, and it also removes the latent hazard on the two card components.

Whether `vite build` in this repo's exact plugin load order resolves @vue/compiler-core's PROD bundle — strongly indicated (Vite sets NODE_ENV before plugin resolution, and both the prod parser default `comments: false` and the absence of DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT are verified in node_modules), but not observed on a real build artifact. This is the one hinge under my downgrade of P-1's production severity.
superlatives: The keyset-pagination protocol in `demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts` is genuinely well built: `currentFilterOpts()` (:52-61) is a single filter builder shared by the fresh load and the cursor continuation "so the two can never drift apart", and the `loadGeneration` monotonic counter (:47, :64, :73, :78, :99, :104) is a correct, minimal stale-response guard with the discard applied on BOTH the success and error paths. Its one defect (the `finally` at :112 scoping the `loadingMore` release to the same guard) is a two-character fix on an otherwise exemplary composable.

`demo/platform/transport/availability.ts` is the best-argued module I read on this axis. It refuses to let a dev-config error masquerade as "backend offline": `detectDevMisconfig` (:112-116) is pure, total and explicitly written for testability; `markApiUnreachable` (:167-172) refuses to downgrade a `misconfigured` latch; the loud message (:119-130) names the page origin, the resolved base URL, the CORS cause and the exact command to run. The whole rationale is written down at :20-35. That this designed diagnosis is then thrown away one layer up (`useBrowsePalettes.ts:79`) is the sharpest thing the C axis found, and it is sharp precisely because the thing being discarded is this good.

`demo/styles/foundation.css:657-696` and `:829-841` — ONE named colour-surface roster, declared once and reused verbatim by both `forced-colors: active` and `@media print`, with `[data-color-surface]` as an explicit extension point and a header comment (:657-661) that states the policy's purpose. This is why D5-01's cure is a single attribute rather than a per-component patch: the architecture was designed to make enrolment cheap, and the omission is an omission, not a missing mechanism.

`vite.config.ts:37-50` generates the value.js self-alias set from `package.json#exports` with per-entry ANCHORED regexes, and the comment above it (:30-36) records the exact prior bug that motivated the anchoring (a string alias prefix-matching `@mkbabb/value.js/math` into a path through the dist FILE). A self-alias table cannot drift from the published export map here, by construction.

`demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteColorStrip.vue:50-71` — the weighted-segment maths applies an 8% legibility floor and then renormalises the floored weights so they still sum to 100%, with a three-level fallback (explicit `weights` → the colours' own `weight` fields → equal widths) and a `Math.max(…, 0.5)` guard against a zero-width segment. Small, correct, and the reasoning is on the page (:38-48).

killed.claim: "The only live-region announcement the commit produces is false … When the save empties the draft and the new palette is filtered out, that status region MOUNTS and announces 'empty plate, No saved palettes yet, Add colors above, then save the set.' A screen-reader user's sole feedback on a successful save is a statement that they own nothing." (challenge-D-design.md:96-102; carried into the one-sentence gestalt at :51-55 and the §C row "undesigned, and actively announces its opposite" at :320.)
killed.refutation: Refuted by the report's own evidence file. probe-D11-pass4.json § P2 records `filtered.emptyText` = "· empty plate ·No saved palettes yet.Add colors above, then save the set." and `after.emptyText` = the byte-identical string, with `filtered.cardCount` = `after.cardCount` = 0. The role="status" region was ALREADY mounted, with that exact text, BEFORE the commit — which is precisely what D4-04 files as its own finding (challenge-D-design.md:264-266, same probe, same section). A live region that neither mounts nor changes its text fires no announcement in any screen reader. So the commit produces NO announcement at all; it does not "announce the opposite", and the screen reader is never "told 'No saved palettes yet'" at the moment of save — it was told that a second earlier, by the filter. The defect is total silence on success, which is a different (and differently-cured) defect from a false announcement. Cite drift compounds it: the role="status" container is demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:28, not :33 as cited. Limbs (a) "the success has no representation at all" (CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:247-265 — emit, blank, emit, no status, no focus move) and (c) focus destruction (the commit button at :134-142 lives inside `v-if="savedColorStrings.length > 0"` at :118 and unmounts itself while focused) are unaffected and stand.

killed.claim: "Edit, Copy, Remove and select are unreachable by pointer, touch, keyboard and AT … A user cannot remove a colour from their own draft by any means." (challenge-D-design.2026-07-28-pass2.md:66-67 gestalt and :189-192); carried into the pass-3 state matrix as "active/pressed (swatch) | unreachable" and "the only path from empty → populated | dead" (challenge-D-design.2026-07-28-pass3.md:325-332).

The three action buttons are real <button> elements with live @click handlers (CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:46, :49, :52) inside a `<Teleport to="body">` panel (SwatchHoverMenu.vue:37-51) whose own `@pointerenter="$emit('cancelLeave')"` cancels the 250 ms close timer (useHoverPopover.ts:32-40, useLeaveTimer.ts:1-8). Nothing about them is inert: the barrier is geometry (`.floating-panel` has no `position` rule, so the computed top/left are ignored and the panel lands ~900 px below the swatch in normal body flow) plus a dwell timer. The precise, defensible claim is "hidden from AT (aria-hidden=\"true\" at SwatchHoverMenu.vue:45), dead on touch (L-12, measured), and practically unreachable by pointer" — not "dead in every modality" and not "no means". The absolutist phrasing was never measured in either direction: probe-D16 used `click({force:true})`, so pointer reachability remains formally UNPROVEN, which is itself the indictment of the claim as filed.

killed.claim: "the edit-overlay Save/Cancel buttons (:75, :78) and the add slot (:100) have no hover scale, no press magnitude and no focus register — and unlike their siblings at :46,:49,:52 they carry no focus-visible rule at all." (challenge-D-design.2026-07-28-pass2.md:601-604; same inversion in challenge-C-implementation.md:444-449 (C-5) and its C-13 row at :75.)
killed.refutation: The comparison is inverted. There is no universal focus reset in the served cascade: every `outline: none` rule in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css is class-scoped (`.goo-blob-hit:focus-visible`, `.disclosure-trigger:focus-visible`, `.field-control:focus-visible`, `.switch:focus-visible`, `.radio-group__item:focus-visible`, `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-thumb:focus-visible`, two `.segmented-dot:focus-visible` — 8 rules, all class-qualified), and `grep -rn "outline: *none"` over demo/styles/*.css returns nothing. So the two bare <button> elements at CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:75 and :78, which carry no focus-visible utility at all, RETAIN the user-agent focus ring. Meanwhile the three siblings at :46, :49 and :52 each write `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40` — they delete the UA ring and replace it with a colour key the theme never mints (see missed finding M1: `--color-ring` is defined nowhere in demo/, src/ or glass-ui). The three buttons the report holds up as having a focus register are the only ones in the file that actively suppress the one ring that works. (:100 is moot — it is the inert span, never focusable.) The MAJOR itself — that `btn-interactive` is a phantom and the hover/press legs were deleted rather than moved, in violation of standing edict 6 — is CONFIRMED and untouched.

missed.claim: `focus-visible:ring-ring/40` is a THIRD phantom in the same family, and it sits inside the very class strings all three axes quoted: `--color-ring` is minted nowhere, so the designed focus ring never paints, while the `focus-visible:outline-none` beside it deletes the only ring that would have.
missed.proof: LIVE: demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:46, :49, :52 each carry `focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring/40`. The demo's @theme block mints exactly six colour keys — demo/styles/foundation.css:104 `--color-gold`, :105 `--color-gold-light`, :136 `--color-card-edge`, :143 `--color-well`, :144 `--color-stage`, :145 `--color-on-stage-chrome` — and no `--color-ring`. Repo-wide, `grep -rn -- "--color-ring|--ring\b" demo/ src/` returns exactly ONE hit and it is a comment: demo/styles/focus-ring.css:11, which records that this exact token "resolved EMPTY" as death (2) of the U-F25 focus-ring defect. glass-ui ships zero `--color-ring` and zero compiled `ring-ring` rules (`grep -c "ring-ring" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.css` → 0); its own register is `.focus-ring` + `--focus-ring-color`/`--focus-ring-shadow` (foundation.css:264 re-points it onto `--accent-live`). WHY IT WAS MISSED: all three axes ran a phantom-class sweep and elevated `.btn-interactive`/`.floating-panel` to MAJOR/BLOCKER on exactly this test (challenge-D-design.2026-07-28-pass2.md:577-604, challenge-C-implementation.md:421-455, challenge-L-library.md:339-382), and all three pasted this class string verbatim while sweeping (challenge-C-implementation.2026-07-27-pass1.md:470, …pass3-prior.md:525) — but every sweep tested CSS CLASS names and none tested THEME KEYS, so a phantom that lives one layer down went through untouched. The standing rule it violates is docs/precepts/instructions/LESSONS-LEARNED.md Q-chron-4 invariant 33 (fleet-wide corpus grep before retiring a class/token); the mechanical gate that rule names, `scripts/proof-phantom-classes.mjs`, does not exist in value.js — it is glass-ui-side only (the `.retired-classes.txt` registry lives in .claude/worktrees/glass-ui-pinned/), which is why the C axis's cure proposes building a walk the fleet already specified.

killed.claim: "The palette-name collision rule has two homes with THREE semantic divergences — the store filters isLocal, the component does not; the store also requires colorsMatch, the component does not; the two disagree." (MAJOR)
killed.refutation: The isLocal leg is FALSE. The component never sees a non-local palette: usePaletteStore.ts:51-55 defines `savedPalettes = computed(() => getStore().value.palettes.filter((p): p is Palette & { id: string } => p.isLocal && p.id != null))`, and that is exactly what the parent hands down (PalettesPane.vue:45 :saved-palettes="pm.savedPalettes.value"). The component's predicate over a pre-filtered array is behaviourally identical to isLocal && name-match. The colorsMatch leg is not a divergence either: the two answer different questions by design — the component asks "does a palette with this NAME exist?" (to offer Update instead of minting a twin), the store asks "is this the EXACT same palette?" (to dedupe-and-move-to-front). Neither is wrong on its own terms and there is no input on which they contradict. What survives is narrower and belongs at MINOR: (a) a name-identity rule living in a leaf editor rather than the store, costing a 23-field Palette[] prop for one .find(); and (b) a genuine side effect the axis missed — because the component blocks any name collision first, createPalette's own dedupe branch (usePaletteStore.ts:67-77) is unreachable from onCurrentPaletteSaved, i.e. dead on this path.

confirmed.claim: Activating the slot action destroys the control that hosts it; EmptyState publishes no focus contract.

killed.id: L-N7 (the `| undefined` half, and its cure)
killed.claim: "`tsconfig.base.json:13` sets `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`; writing `?: string | undefined` re-admits explicit `undefined` and cancels that flag across this component's entire prop surface. Cure: adopt the destructure form, drop every `| undefined`."
killed.refutation: Two errors, one of them a cure that would break the build. (1) Citation: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true` is at tsconfig.base.json:11, not :13 (line 13 is `useDefineForClassFields`). (2) The cure is structurally unsound. PaletteCardGrid.vue:38-44 declares `emptyText?: string` / `emptyEyebrow?: string` / `emptyHint?: string` and forwards them at :24-26 as `:message="emptyText"` / `:eyebrow="emptyEyebrow"` / `:hint="emptyHint"`. Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` an optional-without-`| undefined` target CANNOT accept a `string | undefined` source, so dropping `| undefined` from EmptyState.vue:74-88 makes those three bindings type errors in the demo program. The `| undefined` is load-bearing at the one wrapper the same report calls a rename (L-7) — the two findings collide and L-N7 loses. Note also that C-N5 and D-N4 reach the right verdict for the wrong reason: they say the flag *requires* `| undefined`, which is backwards (the flag's purpose is that `?: T` excludes undefined). What requires it is the forwarding call site. The idiom-fork half of L-N7 (withDefaults vs destructure) survives and is confirmed separately as C-9.

killed.claim: "`AdminUsersPanel.vue` `<Transition>` present ✔ · `MixSourceSelector.vue` `<Transition>` present ✔ … 4 of 7 hosts hard-cut."
killed.refutation: Both ✔ rows are mis-attributed; the correct figure is 1 of 8, not 3 of 7. AdminUsersPanel.vue's only `<Transition>` is at :16-20, `name="vj-celebrate"`, wrapping the prune-result `<span v-if="pruneResult">` in the panel header — nowhere near the plate. Its actual species chain at :46 (`v-if="loading"`), :51/:52 (`v-else-if="loadError"`), :63 (`v-else-if="users.length === 0"`), :64 (`v-else`) is a bare v-if chain with no transition at all. MixSourceSelector.vue has a `<TransitionGroup>` at :120 inside the *colors* mode branch; its EmptyState sits at :239 in the *palettes* branch with no transition wrapping it. Counting BrowsePane and PaletteCardGrid, exactly one of eight hosts transitions the plate. The finding's direction is strengthened by the correction — which is why it is confirmed above and only the table is killed.

killed.claim: "EmptyState's own contribution is the load-bearing half: it hosts, inside the `#action` slot of a conditionally-rendered root, the one control whose activation unmounts that root."
killed.refutation: Nothing in the mechanism is owned by the subject. The `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` is BrowsePane.vue:40; the colliding `key="error"` is BrowsePane.vue:63; the predicate is BrowsePane.vue:62; the handler is BrowsePane.vue:73 `@click="pm.loadRemotePalettes()"`. EmptyState.vue contributes a `<slot name="action" />` at :26 and nothing else — it does not key itself, does not transition, and does not choose its own mount condition. The report itself concedes "Only BrowsePane sits inside a `<Transition>` today," and I verified that concession is exact: every other host has zero `<Transition>` around the plate (see the D-21 kill). A BLOCKER whose entire causal chain lives in a different component is mis-homed, and homing it here risks the real BrowsePane defect being closed by an EmptyState edit that cannot touch it. (The underlying blank-pane behaviour is not disputed — it is simply not decidable from this read-only seat; see unproven.)

killed.id: L-1 cure ("delete `tag=` at all 18 sites") + its site count
killed.claim: "value.js … left the old prop in place at 18 bindings across 9 files. Cure: delete `tag=` at all 18 sites (mechanical, zero-delta at the 15 decorative ones). … three shipped affordances are dead."
killed.refutation: Wrong in three directions at this HEAD. (a) The count is stale and low: `grep -rn 'tag="' demo/ | wc -l` → 26, across 13 files. (b) The blanket cure is over-broad — PaletteSlugBar.vue:9 passes `tag="form"` to `<SearchBar>`, a different component entirely, and GenerateControls.vue:193 is a comment. Deleting "all" would strike a live binding on a component that does own a `tag` prop. The correct live figure is 24 `tag="div|button"` bindings on WatercolorDot, which is what docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §4.2 already books: "W17 owns the live exhaustive manifest—currently 25 explicit `tag=\"div|button\"` calls." The item is a *booked wave*, not an unowned residue — framing it as "the consumer did not migrate" omits that the canon already scheduled it. (c) "Three shipped affordances are dead" is an undercount by half — see missed.

killed.claim: "The error register has THREE implementations, not two — `demo/scenes/about/markdown/Markdown.vue:19-30` renders `<Alert><AlertTitle class=\"font-display text-heading\">`, and its own comment admits the copy."
killed.refutation:
Overstated by category. I read Markdown.vue:19-30 whole: it is `
Oh snap...We couldn't find the documentation…
` — a glass-ui `Alert` primitive with no glyph, no `detail` line, no `#action`/retry, no plate wrapper, no `.plate-ink`, and none of the four drifted geometry numbers that make L-3/D-14 a real fork. What is actually duplicated is ONE class pair, `font-display text-heading`, which is precisely D-13's blast radius (four sites: EmptyState:20, EmptyState:58, ErrorBoundary:24, Markdown:26) and is already counted there. Calling it a third implementation of the error PLATE double-counts D-13 as an L-3 escalation and would drag a documentation-not-found notice into a `FailurePlate` refactor it does not belong in. D-14's "a fourth geometry" has the same problem. Downgrade to: a fourth site of the D-13 type-matrix breach.

killed.claim: "Two Button sources coexist: `demo/ui/button/index.ts` (local shadcn) and glass-ui's published `./button` … The shadcn tree is a standing sanctioned structure (~178 files, DO NOT modify)."
killed.refutation: False at this HEAD, and worth recording because the r1 file is still dated evidence in the corpus and the ~178-file shadcn claim also survives in project memory. `cat demo/ui/button/index.ts` is one line: `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. There is exactly one Button source. `find demo/ui -name "*.vue" | wc -l` → 0 across all nineteen directories; every barrel is a pure glass-ui re-export. There is no local shadcn implementation left to protect. Pass 2's N-4 already self-corrects this, and my read confirms N-4 and refutes r1.

killed.claim: "The oracle certifies the state the prop exists to prevent … `dots` is not under-used — it is FORBIDDEN to be used on the only plate where it would apply."
killed.refutation: The conclusion (dots is dead) is right; this particular argument for it is the weakest of the four and should not be the one carried. e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:259-262 is a test assertion, not a ruling — a test is an artefact the same wave that deletes the prop may edit, so "forbidden" overstates what it establishes. The finding is already overdetermined by (a) zero call sites, verified, and (c) structural unreachability through PaletteCardGrid.vue:38-44, verified — either alone is conclusive and neither depends on reading a spec file as law. Carry (a)+(c); drop (d) to context.

missed.claim: `WatercolorDot` in glass-ui 7.0.0 renders NO default slot, yet demo call sites pass children into it — those children are silently discarded. This is the second, unexamined channel of the exact boundary break all three axes reported as `tag=`.
missed.proof: The bundle is dispositive: `grep -c "renderSlot\|_ctx.\$slots" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js` → 0, and the render function's children array is literally `[svg-filter-host, (variant==='ghost' ? ghost-stroke-span : comment)]` — no slot outlet anywhere. Two live sites pass children anyway: demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:95-105 wraps `<Plus class="w-5 h-5 text-primary/60" aria-hidden="true" />` (the add-slot's "+" glyph) inside the dot; demo/shell/dock/Dock.vue:271-281 wraps an entire `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` plus the routed `<component :is="viewManager.currentConfig.value.icon" class="dock-seal-ink">` — the collapsed dock seal's ink — inside it. Vue drops children a component never renders, so both are dead markup. challenge-L (L-1, N-6), challenge-C (C-5) and challenge-D (D-15) all examined this producer at this version and all three read only the props table.

missed.claim: `PaletteCardGrid`'s `emptyAction` slot is dead — declared with a `$slots` guard that can never be true — so the empty species ships with no CTA at any site in the app, contradicting the component's own documented contract.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:28-29 `<template v-if="$slots.emptyAction" #action><slot name="emptyAction" /></template>`. `grep -rn "emptyAction" demo/` returns exactly those two lines and nothing else — zero hosts fill it (BrowsePane.vue:80-91 and PalettesPane.vue:75-80 are its only two consumers and neither passes it). Cross-checked from the other side: `grep -rn "#action" demo/` outside EmptyState.vue yields BrowsePane:68, AdminAuditPanel:48, AdminUsersPanel:57, AdminTagsPanel:74, AdminFlaggedPanel:28, AdminNamesPanel:36 and :86 — every single one is on `variant="error"`. So EmptyState.vue:9 ("optional hint + CTA slot") and :64 `<slot name="action" />` describe an affordance the empty plate never receives. Pass-1 D had this as its BLOCKER D-1 (challenge-D-design.pass1.md:49); pass-2 D dropped it entirely and pass-2 L's L-7 catalogued the four `empty*` props without noticing the fifth forwarded member is inert.

missed.claim: `PaletteCardGrid`'s `role="list"` has no `listitem` children in ANY state, not just the empty one — the populated children are `role="article"`.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 `role="list"`; its only other child is `<slot />` at :12, filled by `<PaletteCard>` from BrowsePane.vue:92 and PalettesPane.vue:81, whose root carries `role="article"` at demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:22 (the grid's own comment at :7 says so out loud: "each child PaletteCard (role=\"article\") sits in a list landmark"). ARIA 1.2 `list` requires owned `listitem`; `article` is not one. C-3 (challenge-C-implementation.md:132-152) found the empty-state half via a live probe that only saw `childRoles: ["status"]` and concluded the atom's hard-coded role was the mechanism — but the container is malformed with or without EmptyState, which changes the cure: the fix is at the grid, not only at the atom.

missed.claim: The `--ink-muted` masking fallback is a nine-file pattern with an inconsistent posture, and one consumer pipes the ink-guarded token into a graphics slot — the same category error D-4 flags for the mark, at a site no axis looked at.
missed.proof: L-6 and L-N3 scope the problem to the five `.plate-ink` definers. The token read is wider: `grep -rn -- "--ink-muted" demo/` shows `var(--ink-muted, var(--muted-foreground))` also at ConfigSliderPane.vue:205, ColorComponentDisplay.vue:200, :205, :211, ColorSpaceSelector.vue:309 and PaneHeader.vue:123 — nine consumers of the masking fallback, not five. Posture is not uniform: ParseEchoReadout.vue:38 and :44 read `var(--ink-muted)` with NO fallback at all, so the identical token has two different failure semantics in one tree. And ConfigSliderPane.vue:202 sets `--slider-track-bg: var(--ink-muted, var(--muted-foreground));` — feeding a token that is contrast-guarded FOR TEXT into a track-paint slot, which is exactly the producer-seam error challenge-D-design.md:218-247 (D-4) presses against `--accent-live` on the mark. Whatever cure lands must move nine sites, not five, and must decide the ParseEchoReadout posture.

missed.claim: `demo/shared/utils.ts` exports a `cn()` helper with zero call sites; it is the sole reason `clsx` and `tailwind-merge` appear in `demo/shared/`'s outbound edge set.
missed.proof: demo/shared/utils.ts:1-6 imports `clsx` + `twMerge` and exports `cn`. `grep -rn "\bcn(" demo/ --include=*.vue --include=*.ts | wc -l` → 1, and that one hit is the definition itself; no file imports the symbol (every `shared/utils` importer — GradientCodeEditor.vue:3, useColorParsing.ts:2, useColorUrl.ts:8, useColorNameResolution.ts:2, useColorPersistence.ts:3, useColorPipeline.ts:2, useAtmosphere.ts:33 — takes only `debounce`). challenge-L-library.md's negative proof 1 enumerates `clsx` and `tailwind-merge` as demo/shared's outbound edges and passes them as clean, and L-10 waves at "cn() retirement already booked" without ever measuring that the export is dead today. Two dependencies and a public helper are live purely as residue.

missed.claim: `EmptyState.vue:55`'s `uppercase` utility is redundant against the producer utility it sits on.
missed.proof: EmptyState.vue:55 reads `class="text-mono-caption uppercase tracking-[0.18em] plate-ink"`. glass-ui's `dist/styles/typography/utilities.css` defines `@utility text-mono-caption { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: var(--type-caption); letter-spacing: var(--type-tracking-caps); text-transform: uppercase; }` — the casing is already in the role. D-16 (challenge-D-design.md:540-545) caught the `tracking-[0.18em]` literal on this exact line and read the utility's definition to price the override at 2.58912px, but did not notice the class beside it is a no-op. Small, but it is dead code on the line the audit already opened.

missed.claim: `aria-hidden="true"` on the trio wrapper is redundant — the producer already sets it on every dot, unconditionally, in the shipped bundle.
missed.proof: EmptyState.vue:43 `aria-hidden="true"` on the `[data-slot="empty-state-trio"]` div. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js emits `o("span", {"aria-hidden": "true", …})` as a hard-coded literal on the root of every dot, and again on the ghost-stroke child span. challenge-L-library.pass1.md:126-127 noted this in passing; pass 2 — which GOVERNS the axis — dropped it, and neither C's N-7 ("the mark is properly hidden from AT … No finding") nor D's N-7 registered that the hiding is doubled. Harmless today, but it is one of the small dependencies on producer behaviour that the `tag=` migration should sweep in the same pass.

unproven: C-1's blank-pane end state (challenge-C-implementation.md:24-104) — Retry on /#/browse leaving the transition host with zero element children, persisting across hash navigation. All static preconditions VERIFIED (BrowsePane.vue:40 `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">`, :62 predicate, :63 `key="error"`, :73 `@click="pm.loadRemotePalettes()"`; Vue 3.5.35), but whether Vue 3.5's BaseTransition `afterLeave` re-entry recovers is not decidable from source — its out-in path does force an update on leave completion, which is the opposite of what the report observes. killed.claim: BLOCKER — "activating Retry annihilates the Browse pane; the re-entering vnode carries the same key=\"error\" as the vnode still leaving, the pending enter is dropped and nothing is ever mounted", filed as an EmptyState defect.
killed.refutation: TWO independent refutations. (1) THE MECHANISM IS WRONG, decidable statically against the installed runtime. Vue 3.5.35, node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:1384-1386: `if (state.isLeaving) { return emptyPlaceholder(child); }` executes BEFORE `getInnerChild`, before `resolveTransitionHooks` and before any `isSameVNodeType` comparison — so during the 200ms leave the re-flip to `key=\"error\"` never reaches a key comparison at all, and the same-key collision the report describes cannot occur. At :1411-1418 the out-in branch installs `leavingHooks.afterLeave = () => { state.isLeaving = false; if (!(instance.job.flags & 8)) { instance.update(); } }` — an UNCONDITIONAL forced re-render when the leave completes. At that update `instance.subTree` is the Comment placeholder, so the guard at :1403 (`oldInnerChild.type !== Comment`) is false and the error vnode is returned for normal mount. The runtime has an explicit recovery path the report's narrative denies exists. (2) THE ATTRIBUTION IS WRONG. The `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` is at /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:40, the 47ms failure round-trip is at /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:63-88, and the report itself concedes at challenge-C-implementation.md:89-91 that "Only BrowsePane sits inside a `<Transition>` today, so only BrowsePane reaches the blank-pane end state." /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue contains no transition, no key, no lifecycle and no async — hosting a slot inside a `v-if` root is not a defect, it is what every conditionally-rendered component does. This is a BrowsePane defect filed under EmptyState, and the prescribed cure ("give EmptyState a stable root that never unmounts") would rebuild the atom to work around a host's transition mode — and would DIRECTLY CONTRADICT the same report's own N-4 (challenge-C-implementation.md:349-355), which proves the two-root replacement is what makes the species swap audible to AT. The cure trades a confirmed a11y property for an unconfirmed symptom. The observed blank pane may well be real; it is carried in `unproven` as a host-level item, and it must not be closed by editing this component.

Glass earns its blur by revealing live content; otherwise it is a neutral well' — and `:16`, which defines the well tier as an 'opaque/quiet neutral stage' whose 'specimen supplies color'. One sentence of static prose reveals nothing and earns no blur. This is the *cause* of what D-6 measured as a 1.20:1 'hue-only stain': the D seat read the pixels and blamed shadcn (K-1); the mechanism is a glass component conscripted as a well, with three call-site overrides that a non-resolving `cn` lets silently lose. missed.claim: M-G · Wrapping static data rows in a `TooltipTrigger` silently enrols them in a reduced-motion carve-out written for overlays — and the hovered and resting states then take different PRM rules.
missed.proof: `demo/styles/animations.css:184-192` is the blanket guard (`transition-duration: 0.01ms !important` on `*`). `:200-211` then re-grants, at equal specificity and later source order, `transition-duration: 150ms !important; transition-property: opacity !important` to `[data-state="open"]`, `[data-state="closed"]` — with an explicit scope statement in its comment: 'The global guard above is too blunt for reka-ui Dialog/Sheet/Popover overlays.' missed.claim: M-I · The contrast referent is a chroma-blind scalar: the guard certifies against `oklch(L, 0, 0)` — a neutral grey — while the ink actually paints on a chromatic plate. This is the real residual behind D-11's light-arm shortfall.
missed.proof: `demo/color-session/ink.ts:56-61` `surfaceColor(L)` returns `oklch(L, 0, 0, 1)`, and `:69-79` `certify()` passes exactly that to `safeAccentColor(accent, surfaceColor(surfaceL), {minimumRatio, gamut})`. So however well `resolveSurfaceLightness` composites the live probed tint with the live ambient (and it does so genuinely — see K-4 and the superlative below), the *value it produces is one number*: an OKLab lightness. WCAG relative luminance is a function of all three sRGB primaries, and a chromatic ground and a neutral grey of equal OKLab L do not share it. The guard therefore walks to its 5.75 target against a surface that does not exist. This is a narrower and more actionable statement than D-11's — which blamed a static tint model that was already retired, and computed the target wrong (K-4, K-5) — and it explains why the two survive together: the mechanism D-11 named is fixed, the outcome it measured is not. The fix is in the referent's *type*, not in the probe: `resolveSurfaceLightness` should return a colour, not a lightness. Filed as a design-integrity finding because it silently caps the certification quality of every accent-ink consumer in the app, not just this component.

Accepted as consistent. D-17's own conclusion is the modest one — that this file makes no reduced-motion decision at all — which is source-true. See M-G for what it missed.
superlatives: THE F-3 FILL/INK SPLIT (`ColorNutritionLabel.vue:190-208`). The comment records the exact defect it repairs — 'a foreground-certified value reused as a BACKGROUND fill, leaving the fixed `--foreground` ink uncertified on top (measured 1.57:1 at the owner's own color, light mode)' — and the repair is structurally right: the TEXT role certifies against the tier it sits on (`useSafeAccentFn("resting")`), the FILL role derives its ink from the fill's OWN luminance (`contrastInkFor`). Two roles, two guards, correctly separated. Even the D seat, which was hunting, conceded it (challenge-D-design.md:807-810: 'the F-3 fill/ink split at `:204-208` does exactly what its comment claims'). C-2's defect is the `?? ""` bolted onto the end of it, not the idea.

THE LIVE TIER PROBE (`demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts`). This is the best engineering I read in the whole surface. To answer 'what lightness is my ink actually sitting on', it inserts a hidden element into the document's own cascade, resolves the rung's background token — `color-mix`, tint knob and all — to a concrete colour+alpha via dual-ground canvas draws, and composites it with the live ambient. It then solves the two hard problems that idea creates: an `probeEpoch` ref bumped from every consumer's `onMounted`, because 'a consumer's first `computed` evaluation runs while Vue is still building the subtree DETACHED … and the cached computed would carry the static-model referent FOREVER (the resume-run's earned catch: certified against the model's 0.90 while the REAL band composited 0.75 — 3.59:1 measured)'; and a scheme/epoch-scoped cache, because an uncached probe 'would interleave `getComputedStyle` + canvas readbacks with the boot writer's per-frame root `setProperty` writes — a forced style recalc EVERY drag frame.' It degrades to the static model only in jsdom. D-11 attacked the model this replaced (K-4) and never saw the instrument.

`PICKER_CHANNELS ... satisfies Record<SpaceId, readonly ChannelMeta[]>` (`demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:70`). Total by construction — which is why the Components rows are the only correct rows on the five broken cards. The counter-example, `colorSpaceInfo`'s bare `as const` (`colorSpaceInfo.ts:334`), sits in the same directory describing the same 17 spaces. Having the right pattern and the wrong pattern ten lines apart is what makes L-1's cure obviously right and cheap; the corpus is correct to converge on it three times.

THE COMMENT LEDGER. Nearly every non-obvious line in `ColorNutritionLabel.vue` carries the wave id, the finding id, and the measured number that motivated it: `:2-3` (three-voice law, R.W3 Lane A/A1), `:5-7` (AB-3, T.W8 remediation_1 · D1), `:21-25` (S.W4-8, why the 'Type:' row died — 'One sentence, said once'), `:104-108` (the well-row idiom with its named precedent, VersionHistoryDrawer), `:118-120`, `:190-208`. Provenance this dense is rare and it is why three independent seats could argue about this file precisely rather than vaguely. It is also, honestly, the file's biggest liability: `:5-7` asserts a material the component does not have (M-A), and a comment that confident is believed.

`AboutPane.vue:31-41`. A hard-won lesson recorded exactly: 'glass-ui's slim `cn` does not conflict-resolve, so an axis utility sorts earlier and silently LOSES the cascade (the former `py-[1.618rem]` here never painted — the card's cqi default did; the W4 seed-rider-2 clause, generalized).' It names the mechanism, the symptom, the specific dead declaration and the clause that generalizes it. That paragraph is what let me find M-A — the identical pathology, unfixed, in the child component one line below it.
