killed.claim: '31 sub-24 px targets; this pane IS the app's tap-target outlier. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 asks for ≥24×24 CSS px and has no pointer-type exemption.'
killed.refutation: REFUTED as an SC 2.5.8 failure. The seat cites the wrong half of the SC: 2.5.8 has an explicit **Spacing** exception — undersized targets pass when a 24 CSS px diameter circle centred on each bounding box does not intersect another target's circle. Here the thumbs are 12 wide × 24 tall (mechanically entailed by the producer recipe: glass-ui.css `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-thumb{width:calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*.75)}` = 12px and `.slider-track{height:calc(var(--slider-thumb-size,1rem)*1.5)}` = 24px at the default `md` rung), one per row, with no horizontal neighbour anywhere on the row. Vertical pitch: demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:215-217 floors the row at `clamp(2rem, 7cqi, 2.625rem)`, and the row's own composition (producer `configurator-row flex flex-col gap-1.5` + the demo's `py-1`, ConfigSliderPane.vue:142) stacks a header line, a 6px gap and the 24px track — so adjacent thumb centres are ≥38px apart at the clamp floor and ~60px in practice, far beyond the 24px circles. The exception is satisfied and the SC is met. What survives is an ergonomics observation (a 12px-wide grab handle is thin), not a conformance failure — and challenge-C's own severity (MAJOR) and cure ('root-level … unconditional 24px hit area') are argued from a floor that does not bind. Note also that the corpus's supporting datum — the visual report's 'smallTapTargets: 39' — is a raw <24px census, not an SC 2.5.8 verdict; challenge-L §7 correctly declines to charge it, so the corpus contradicts itself here.

killed.claim: 'The live readout violates the NORMATIVE card-lock law on both required mechanisms' — mechanism 1 being absent `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on all 31 readouts.
killed.refutation: REFUTED on mechanism 1, and the framing rests on a truncated quotation. (a) demo/DESIGN.md:64-65 reads 'Two mechanisms, both required wherever live numeric values render **at display scale**:' — challenge-D-design.md:352-355 quotes it as '…wherever live numeric values render:', dropping the scope qualifier that is doing all the work. The subject is an 11px `text-micro` readout, not a display-scale hero number. (b) The law's own mechanism-1 text (demo/DESIGN.md:67-70) states: '**Fira Code is tabular by default**; Fraunces is NOT — a Fraunces-set number MUST declare `tabular-nums`.' The readout is Fira Code: the producer renders the `name` slot as `truncate text-micro **font-mono** text-muted-foreground/70` (glass-ui configurator-M5OaIlJd.js:196-199). A computed `font-variant-numeric: normal` on a tabular-by-default face is therefore compliant with the cited law, not a violation of it. (c) The card-lock law's operative requirement is that 'a value change may never move the card … changes NO containing card rect (±0px)'; the `name` span is the last item in a left-aligned inner flex row (`flex min-w-0 items-baseline gap-2`, same chunk :195), so its 27px width swing moves neither the card nor the label's left edge. What survives is real but smaller: `fmt` (ConfigSliderPane.vue:84-86) makes the number change KIND mid-drag (`1.900 → 1.950 → 2 → 2.050`), and the swing can re-trigger the sibling label's `truncate` in a narrow pane. That is a MINOR format-stability defect against VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:78, not a MAJOR breach of a NORMATIVE card-lock law.

killed.claim: 'A text token used as a fill … ConfigSliderPane is the **only** site that paints `--ink-muted` as a background.'
killed.refutation: FALSE as stated, and by the very file challenge-D cites two paragraphs later as the correct idiom. demo/workbenches/extract/ExtractControls.vue:75 sets `:style="{ '--slider-track-bg': trackInk }"` on its sliders and :22 sets `backgroundColor: trackInk` on the rail — and `trackInk` (:123-125) is `cssColor ? safeCss(cssColor, GRAPHICS_CONTRAST_FLOOR) : "var(--ink-muted)"`, i.e. literally `var(--ink-muted)` painted as a background whenever no live pick threads. So the app has at least two sites painting the token as a fill, through the identical mechanism; the difference is that one has a chromatic branch. The genuine finding — that the config console pins the degenerate branch permanently, so the Colour section's chromatic axes render achromatic while the Picker's Lab channels are full ramps — survives; the 'only site' superlative and the 'a text token used as a fill' novelty do not.

killed.claim: 'The declared variant is defeated' — `variant="spectrum"` is requested at ConfigSliderPane.vue:146 and then overridden, so 'the control announces the spectrum recipe and paints none of it'; filed as an 'Owner edict 5 violation (root-level styling, never per-instance override)'.
killed.refutation: REFUTED. The producer's spectrum recipe IS `background: var(--slider-track-bg, var(--secondary))` on `.slider-track` (glass-ui.css, `.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-track`) — the custom property is the published consumer door, not a defeat of it, and the caller has always been the one who supplies the track material (the Picker channels and Extract do the same). Likewise `.slider-range{background:0 0}` is the spectrum recipe's OWN author declaration — the range is transparent by design, not because the demo left it unpainted; ConfigSliderPane.vue:197-200 already says so in its comment. The edict-5 charge is contradicted inside the same corpus: challenge-L-library.md:448-451 rules this exact line 'correct by contrast: a custom-property handoff, not a selector reach. That is the pattern the other three should follow.' The defensible finding is different and sharper (see missed): the pane chose the wrong VARIANT — `spectrum` is the recipe with no filled range, so 31 non-chromatic scalar controls lose the fill affordance the `standard` variant would give.

killed.claim: 'Retire the track override. Delete `--slider-track-bg: var(--ink-muted…)` and let the `spectrum` variant paint what it declares — a real `.slider-range` restores the value signal … and makes the WHCM roster entry at foundation.css:693 protect something that exists. Kills D-5, D-6.'
killed.refutation: STRUCTURALLY UNSOUND, twice. (i) Deleting the custom property cannot produce a `.slider-range` fill: the transparency is hard-declared in the producer's scoped CSS (`.glass-slider[data-variant=spectrum] .slider-range{…background:0 0}`), which no consumer property touches. The cure's stated benefit is unreachable by the stated means. (ii) Deleting it reverts the track to the recipe fallback `var(--secondary)` — precisely the material that e2e/smoke/oracles/o18-contrast-census.spec.ts:1147-1161 measured at ≈1.09:1 light / 1.26:1 dark against the well and gates born-RED under WCAG 1.4.11 (the measurement is recorded in situ at ConfigSliderPane.vue:190-201). killed.claim: 'focused | weak | `outline: none`; focus is a 2 px box-shadow at 30% alpha … barely separable from the thumb outline' — booked without qualification in the state-coverage matrix.
killed.refutation: INCOMPLETE, and it omits a guard the same report cites elsewhere. Under forced colors, demo/styles/foundation.css:700-720 binds `:where(a[href], button, [role="button"], …, [role="slider"], …):focus-visible { outline: 2px solid Highlight; outline-offset: 2px; }` at zero specificity — so slider focus DOES survive WHCM with a real system outline, the one register in which a box-shadow ring cannot paint. killed.claim: 'Propagation. `geometry`/`surface`/`color` are re-spread into **plain** snapshot objects inside the computed, while `membrane`, `satellites` and `interaction` pass through as the live `reactive` proxy. The one slider that works (`membrane.smoothK`) is on the proxy side.'
killed.refutation: REFUTED, and inverted. Object-spreading a Vue `reactive` inside a `computed` READS each key and therefore TRACKS it: `{...appBlobConfig.geometry}` (HeroBlob.vue:160-166) registers every geometry member as a dependency, so a geometry/surface/color write invalidates the computed and yields a fresh object — which HeroBlob.vue:64-66 documents as 'exactly the wake-repaint shape the producer built for'. The proxy-passed atoms (`membrane`, `satellites`, `interaction`) are the ones whose member writes do NOT invalidate the computed — the identity is unchanged, so no prop-change repaint fires at all. The seat's theory therefore predicts the opposite of its own numbers, and its own table falsifies it: `Warp` (membrane.warpAmp — proxy side) reads 5px = null, while `Hue Range`, `Core Glow` and `Iridescence` (colour/surface — snapshot side, and NOT literal-overridden) also read ≤7px. One explanation covers all nine nulls uniformly and is independently proven: the idle park (BPC-2). The 'snapshot vs proxy' half is a red herring that would send a repair at the wrong seam; drop it and BPC-1 stands cleanly on root 1 (the literals), which needs no measurement.

killed.claim: "The only live-region announcement the commit produces is FALSE… that status region **mounts** and announces *'empty plate, No saved palettes yet, Add colors above, then save the set.'* A screen-reader user's sole feedback on a successful save is a statement that they own nothing… This one is explicit and wrong, which is worse than absent." killed.refutation: Refuted by the report's own cited evidence. In `probe-D11-pass4.json` the `role="status"` region was ALREADY mounted before the commit and its text is byte-identical after it: `P2.filtered.emptyText` = `"· empty plate ·No saved palettes yet.Add colors above, then save the set."` and `P2.after.emptyText` = the same string; `P2.filtered.cardCount: 0` and `P2.after.cardCount: 0`. An already-present `role="status"` node whose text does not change does not re-announce — ARIA live regions fire on content mutation, not on unrelated state change elsewhere. So the commit produces NO announcement at all, which is arm (a)'s silence, not "the opposite of what happened". The DOM confirms the mechanism cannot fire in this repro either: `demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:28` (not `:33`, which is a comment line) is the `role="status"` div, and it is gated by `PalettesPane.vue:77` on `filteredSaved.length === 0` — a predicate that was already true before the save. The BLOCKER survives on arms (a) and (c); its headline gestalt sentence ("the screen reader **is told** 'No saved palettes yet'", :53) is not supported — the text is merely present on screen, which is D4-04's finding, not a live-region lie.

The fill/radius legs do hold (`demo/styles/foundation.css:143` `--color-well: var(--well-bg)` is the same token `.dashed-well` uses at `utils.css:105`), but no cited law forbids equal fill. Separately, the cure's gotcha at `:246` — "`utils.css:103` already claims… *'The dashed edge ALONE carries the in-progress semantics'* — and then the very next line adds `box-shadow`" — is a truncated quotation: `demo/styles/utils.css:103-104` reads in one sentence "The dashed edge ALONE carries the in-progress semantics; **the chip cartoon rung stays.**" The comment explicitly retains the stamp it is accused of contradicting.

killed.claim: The measured well-height column "12 → 274.6 px" and "50 → 456.6 px", attributed to `probe-D10-pass4.json` (challenge-D-design.md:154-155)
killed.refutation: Neither number appears in the cited artifact, and one is off by ~194 px. `probe-D10-pass4.json` reports `P1_n12.wellH: 261.4`, `P1_n50.wellH: 650.8`, `P1_n51.wellH: 650.8`, `P1_n80.wellH: 910.4`. The report also assigns 650.8 exclusively to the 51 row when the probe shows 650.8 for BOTH 50 and 51. Only the 80-row (910.4, the load-bearing one) is reproducible. The finding survives — the true n=50 height is 650.8, worse than the report claims — but its geometry table is not reproducible from its own evidence and must not be carried into a wave as measured fact.

killed.claim: "`VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md §3` law 2 caps *empty* secondary content at 15 %" applied to a 12-colour populated tray at 200 % zoom (challenge-D-design.md:301-302)
killed.refutation: Mis-application, and the report italicises the disqualifying word itself. `docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:26` law 2 reads: "**Empty** secondary content occupies at most a narrow invitation tray (≤15% of the stage) or disappears." The 57.6 % measurement was taken with 12 colours seeded (`probe-D10-pass4.mjs` § P4), i.e. a populated tray, which law 2 does not govern. The fallback hook, law 8 at `:34`, forbids competition "through equal size or equal shadow" — it states no viewport-share cap. So the number is real (confirmed above) but no cited law makes 57.6 % a violation. D4-05 should be carried as an UNPROVEN proportion observation, not a MINOR defect, unless a proportion rule for populated secondary content is first ratified.

killed.claim: "the component's **only real `<button>`** is the one with no accessible name" — and "everywhere the component tried to build a button out of a decoration it wrote a careful `aria-label` (`:46`, `:49`, `:52`, `:75`, `:78`, `:101` — six of them)" (challenge-L-library.md:1241-1246)
killed.refutation: False about the source in both limbs. `CurrentPaletteEditor.vue` contains FIVE literal `<button>` elements — `:46`, `:49`, `:52` (Edit/Copy/Remove) and `:75`, `:78` (Save edit / Cancel edit) — plus three glass-ui `Button`s at `:134`, `:151`, `:159`, all of which render `<button>`. Five of the six sites the row lists as "a button built out of a decoration" are genuine `<button>` elements with working `aria-label`s; only `:101` (the `WatercolorDot` add slot) is the decoration. The measurement the row rests on is sound but is a statement about the DOM at rest, not about the source: at rest the swatch-action buttons are teleported out of `.dashed-well` (`SwatchHoverMenu.vue:37-51` `<Teleport to="body">`, and reka-ui teleports `PopoverContent`), the edit-overlay buttons are behind `v-if="isSwatchEditing(i)"` + `hidden lg:flex` (`:58`), and Update/Cancel are behind `v-if="duplicateTarget"` (`:145`) — so the scoped query correctly returns one button. The underlying defect (nameless Save) is CONFIRMED above; the row's title and framing are not carriable.

killed.claim: "**HYPOTHESIS → CONFIRMED.** Two `role="alert"` live regions, byte-identical text, 400 px apart… A screen reader announces the identical alert twice." carried as a MAJOR product defect (challenge-L-library.md:1913, 2136)
killed.refutation: The duplication is unreachable in a shipped build, so it is a dev-server artifact, not a product defect. `demo/shell/dock/DockStatusLamp.vue:31-32` is `const isDev = import.meta.env.DEV; const lamp = computed(() => resolveLampState(availability.value, isDev))`, and `demo/shell/dock/status-lamp.ts:47` opens with `if (!isDev) return null; // dev-gated — the lamp ships dark in production`. In production the lamp never mounts, so only one `role="alert"` can ever exist. The row's own table records the dev gate and then presents the measurement as confirmed product behaviour without the qualification. The genuinely shipped defect in the same area is the inverse and is NOT the one the row headlines: `demo/palettes/browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue:11-16` has **no** dev gate, so a production user can be assertively told ``dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev` `` inside their palette editor. L-21's cure bullet 2 names this; its headline and ledger row do not.

killed.claim: "3 action buttons keep **the strays the file declares retired**, incl. `focus-visible:outline-none`" (challenge-C-implementation.md:75)

The row conflates two unrelated declarations. A real, narrower defect does live at these lines — see the `missed` list — but it is not the one C-13 states.

missed.claim: Pressing Enter in the name field and clicking the on-screen Update button do opposite things from the same visible state — Enter silently re-resolves against the current name and saves correctly, while the banner it leaves on screen still offers to overwrite a palette the user is no longer naming.

missed.claim: There is no way to clear the draft. Once the tray holds colours the only exit that empties it is a commit — abandoning a draft is not an available action.
missed.proof: Exhaustive grep: `grep -rn "emitApply(\[\])" demo/` returns exactly one site, `PalettesPane.vue:53` `@clear-current="colorTarget.emitApply([])"`, and `clearCurrent` is emitted from exactly two places, `CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:264` (`saveCurrentPalette`) and `:275` (`confirmUpdatePalette`). Seventy-five lines later the same file's `:121-124` comment declares dead "the per-instance override list (pill-strip, opaque bg, halved border, **SUPPRESSED focus ring — an a11y regression**)". superlatives: `SwatchHoverMenu.vue:64-66` — `const PANEL_LAYOUT = "p-1.5 flex items-center gap-1"` applied to BOTH the touch `PopoverContent` (`:22`) and the hover Teleport panel (`:43`), with the comment "so the two paths cannot drift". A genuine anti-drift device: one string, two render paths, divergence made structurally impossible. It is the right instinct and it should survive whatever cures the phantom `.floating-panel`.

`CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:292-311` — the `.edit-overlay` block is the most careful CSS in the file. It knows that `demo/styles/utils.css:173-176` sets `--vj-enter-y: 0px; --vj-enter-scale: 0` on `.swatch-row`, that custom properties inherit into descendants, and that the overlay would therefore silently pick up the list's pop geometry; so it re-declares `--vj-enter-x/-y/-scale` and `transform-origin` explicitly and says exactly why in the comment ("the explicit vars also OVERRIDE the .swatch-row list geometry it would otherwise inherit"). Non-obvious, correct, and documented at the point of the fix.

`demo/palettes/browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue:82-91` — the strongest form of reduced-motion gating in the subtree: BOTH the `@keyframes offline-dot-pulse` and the `animation:` declaration live inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so under `reduce` there is nothing to clamp rather than something clamped to 0.01ms. `codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md` §3 records that of thirteen reduced-motion raisers across 46 files, exactly one checked gating at all; this file simply does it. Its two-register status design (`role="alert"` + filled dot for misconfigured vs `role="status"` + open ring for offline, `:11-26`) is likewise a designed, non-colour-only state distinction.

`challenge-D-design.md:336-341` — pass 4's §D negative evidence is a model of adversarial discipline: it verifies that `.edit-overlay`'s containing block IS correct (`SwatchHoverMenu.vue:2-3` gives the slot host `class="relative"`), correctly notes that pass 3 had limited its containing-block claim to the LEAVE transition only, and then explicitly instructs future seats not to over-extend that claim. I independently confirmed both halves (source read plus `probe-D16-pass5.json` → `overlayOffsetParent: "relative"`). An audit that spends a section preventing a future false positive is rarer than one that finds a true one.

`challenge-C-implementation.md:246-292` and `:347-381` (C4-1, C4-3) — the C axis derived its silhouette and hash-collision findings OFFLINE from the producer's own exported PRNG, then matched them against live DOM digit-for-digit. I re-executed the derivation myself from a clean shell and reproduced every value (`""`→turb 173, `"add-current-slot"`→85, `"edit-from-0"`→177, `"edit-to-0"`→128; `rgb(255 0 0)`/`rgb(0 255 0)`/`rgb(0 0 255)` all →173). Evidence that a hostile reader can re-run in one command and confirm to the last decimal is the standard the rest of the corpus should be held to — and C4-3 is correctly routed as a producer relay rather than patched in `demo/`.

`CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:267-272` — `confirmUpdatePalette` opens with `const id = duplicateTarget.value?.id; if (id == null) return;` and a comment naming why (`K-PALID`: only a local, store-backed palette has an id). Honest optional handling with no non-null assertion and no masking fallback, in a function that is otherwise the file's worst defect. The same discipline appears at `:248` (empty guard) and `:249-250` (`.trim() ||` default), and at `demo/palettes/usePaletteActions.ts:95` (`if (palette.id == null) return`) with a comment that explicitly retires a prior dishonest fallback.

`CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:17-21` — the singular/plural count copy (`{{ n }} color{{ n !== 1 ? "s" : "" }}`) carries a comment naming the ruling that produced it ("S.W5-7: singular form — '1 color', never '1 colors'"). It is the one piece of copy in the file that was designed rather than defaulted, and pass 3's own state matrix (challenge-D-design.2026-07-28-pass3.md:343) correctly counts it among the four things that are right.

confirmed.claim: MAJOR — `contain: content` on .palette-card-grid clips the entity card's -3/-5/-7px cartoon caster on its offset (−X) axis, and the last card's bottom leg as well.

PaletteCard.vue:19 adopts `cartoon-surface`, whose only declaration is `box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md)` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css, @utility cartoon-surface), and --shadow-cartoon-md resolves to `-3px 3px 0, -5px 5px 0, -7px 7px 0` (glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css:1) — i.e. 7px of extent on −X and +Y. The two decisions named in the cure (PaletteCard.vue:16-19's deliberate refusal of overflow-hidden to protect the caster, vs PaletteCardGrid.vue:51) are genuinely mutually defeating. confirmed.claim: BLOCKER — one Retry press permanently blanks the Browse pane body; the state machine says 'render the error plate' and the Transition subtree renders nothing.
confirmed.proof: Every structural precondition is in the live tree. BrowsePane.vue:40 `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` sequences three keyed branches (developing :44, error :62, wall :82). Retry calls `pm.loadRemotePalettes()` with no argument (:73), and useBrowsePalettes.ts:63-89 then sets `browsing.value = true` at :66 BEFORE the `await listPalettes(...)` at :72 — Vue's scheduler flush is queued at that assignment and runs ahead of the already-rejected promise's continuation, so a render with key='developing' is guaranteed, the 'error' leave starts, and the catch/finally at :77-88 returns the key to 'error' inside the leave. That is precisely the out-in stranding shape. Corroborated by three independent seats measuring the same blank (pass-1 D-01, pass-2 D-16 two engines, pass-3 P-1 with a DOM dump showing 0 element children and the Transition's `<!---->` anchor). The pane is KeepAlive'd, which explains survival across soft navigation. Cure #3 ('Retry must not re-enter the initial-load state, as the sort path already does with isSort') is confirmed correct by the wiring: the search path calls loadRemotePalettes(true) (usePaletteWiring.ts:159-162), never flips the key, and therefore cannot strand.

confirmed.claim: BLOCKER/MAJOR — two mutually incompatible search predicates composed in series with a handover at 2 characters; slug search is advertised by the client and pre-empted by the server.
confirmed.proof: Client: useBrowsePalettes.ts:43-45 filters `p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || p.slug.includes(q)` through useFilteredList.ts:8-12, which lowercases but does NOT trim (so a leading space is a live predicate). Server gate: useBrowsePalettes.ts:52-61, `...(q.length >= 2 ? { q } : {})` over a TRIMMED q. Server semantics: api/src/modules/palette/service/crud-list.ts:95-96 `if (q) f.$text = { $search: q }` against the single text index api/src/platform/db/db.ts:57-60 `createIndex({ name: "text" }, { name: "palettes_text_name" })` — word/stem matching over `name` only. So substring-over-(name|slug) and whole-word-over-name are neither a narrowing of the other in either direction, the engine that answers changes at a length threshold, and no slug fragment of ≥2 chars can ever reach the client predicate. The 'oc'→0 / 'ocean'→1 cliff is the necessary consequence, not a data accident.

killed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:242-250 — 'trigger: 1 throughout, so the button never disappears from the document; this is NOT the affordance-unmounts story… the node is replaced… which means adding a :disabled state to the button — the obvious patch — would not fix it', and 'loadingBlock: 0 at every frame — the designed pagination skeleton NEVER RENDERED ONCE'.
killed.refutation: Self-contradictory and refuted by the source. useBrowsePalettes.ts:101 sets `loadingMore.value = true` synchronously, before the first await at :103; Vue queues the scheduler flush at that assignment, and it runs before the fetch settles — so the v-if skeleton block (BrowsePane.vue:125-131) NECESSARILY mounts and the v-else-if trigger (:132-144) NECESSARILY unmounts on every activation. Focus cannot move BUTTON→BODY unless the focused node left the document; the pass's own focus transcript is the proof that the branch swapped. `trigger: 1` and `loadingBlock: 0` are sampling artifacts: the first sample is t+30ms and already reads `cards: 6`, i.e. after the whole cycle completed. C pass-2 N-2 (challenge-C-implementation.pass-2-2026-07-28-prior.md:167-193) states the mechanism correctly ('the load-more affordance and its loading state are v-if/v-else-if siblings: pressing the button unmounts the button') and prescribes one persistent node with a label swap + aria-busy — the exact cure D5-02 argues against on false grounds. Net: the focus finding survives (already owned cross-axis); the mechanism paragraph, the 'skeleton never renders' claim and the anti-:disabled argument fall.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:326-348 — 'the defensive tag coercion is the only crash site in the file, and it is STRICTLY LESS SAFE than writing nothing': without the coercion 'Vue logs a dev warning; SearchFilterBar.vue:47 v-if="availableTags.length > 0" reads undefined > 0 → false → the Tags section hides. The pane renders.'
killed.refutation: False for the inputs the finding rests on. SearchFilterBar.vue:147-151 declares `availableTags: Tag[]` as a REQUIRED prop with NO default (plain defineProps, no withDefaults), and the template dereferences it at :47 (`availableTags.length > 0`) and :50 (v-for). Vue substitutes defaults only for `undefined`, and there is none here — so with the coercion deleted and `:available-tags="pm.tagEdit.allTags.value"` bound directly, a `null` or `undefined` payload throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length')` inside SearchFilterBar's render. Both arms crash on that input set; it is not 'strictly wider'. The only input where the un-shimmed path renders is the object-shaped payload — precisely the case the shim was written for, where the shim is an improvement. What survives is narrower and worth keeping: pass-2 N-7 proved the object shape unproducible, and the shim relocates the failure from a leaf child to BrowsePane's entire subtree. The headline comparison should be struck.

killed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:413-447 — 'FOUR type sizes in one 30px metadata row… 20.352 / 18.608 / 16.4 / 11px… items-center on four sizes means the row has NO SHARED BASELINE… the 18.608px is unauthored'.

killed.claim: challenge-D-design-pass1.md:834-846 (MAJOR, never re-litigated by later passes) — 'the route's primary control has no accessible name… placeholder="Search the commons..." is not an accessible name', evidenced as `searchNamed: false` / `nameless: ["INPUT.input-bar-field"]`.

missed.claim: MAJOR — `variant="outline"` is not a prop of glass-ui 7.0.0's Button. Both of the pane's Buttons — the error plate's sole control and the pagination trigger — ship an inert DOM attribute and render at the producer's DEFAULT `emphasis="secondary"`, i.e. the glass-wash/glass-capsule material, on an error plate whose own comment says the plain register drops the conceit. Twelve passes quote this exact line twice and never check the prop.
missed.proof: BrowsePane.vue:69-76 and :136-143 both pass `variant="outline" size="sm" class="font-display"`. The component is glass-ui's: demo/ui/button/index.ts is `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"`, whose root types resolve through dist/index.d.ts:5 → dist/components/button. ButtonProps (dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts) is exactly { emphasis: "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text", tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class } extending PrimitiveProps — there is NO `variant`. The compiled component (dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js, __name:"Button") declares `emphasis: { default: "secondary" }` and paints `data-emphasis`/`data-tone`/`data-size` onto a reka Primitive; `emphasis==="secondary" && tone==="neutral"` adds `glass-wash glass-capsule` + hover. Unknown attrs fall through, and nothing styles them: `grep -o "outline|ghost|data-emphasis" dist/components/button/styles.css` → 11 data-emphasis, 0 outline, 0 ghost; `grep -rn '\[variant' demo/styles demo/**/*.vue` → empty. Blast radius: 51 `<Button>` sites in demo/ pass a `variant` (29 "outline", 28 "ghost" across all components) and the demo passes `emphasis` nowhere, so the whole authored button vocabulary is dead since the 7.0.0 adoption. This is the identical species the mega-tranche already ruled for Skeleton (codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md M-12/M-14: 'surface/variant are not accepted Skeleton props and are inert attrs') — never applied to Button. Typecheck cannot catch it: unknown attributes on a component are legal fallthrough.

missed.claim: MINOR — the search field's only accessible name is a placeholder that vanishes on the first keystroke, and the producer already affords the one-attribute cure the pane never spends. (This is the accurate form of the refuted R2.6.)
missed.proof: BrowsePane.vue:10-14 passes v-model, class and placeholder only. glass-ui's SearchBar declares `inheritAttrs: false` and splits $attrs — `class` onto the wrapper, EVERY OTHER ATTR onto the `<input>` (dist/search.js: `o = computed(() => { let {class:e, ...t} = attrs; return t })`, then `b("input", w({ref…, type:"search"}, o.value, {value, placeholder, class:"input-bar-field"}))`), and its props (dist/components/search/SearchBar.vue.d.ts) carry no aria surface of their own. So `aria-label="Search published palettes"` at the call site lands directly on the input and survives typing, at zero component cost. The producer's sibling primitive shows the intended standard: FuzzySearch defaults `ariaLabel: "Search"` and ships an `sr-only role="status" aria-live="polite"` results announcer (dist/search.js) — the very announcement contract the wall is missing (D-20/R2.5).

missed.claim: MINOR — the pane pins its identity and scrolls its instrument: PaneHeader is sticky, the search + filter surface is not, so on a paginated wall the only discovery control leaves the viewport while the decorative header stays (and keeps scrubbing its scale animation).
missed.proof: demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue:11 — `<div class="pane-header px-4 sm:px-6 pt-4 pb-2 sticky top-0 z-header">` holds the title (:21) and description (:29). BrowsePane.vue:2 makes the Card the scroll host (`pane-scroll-fade … overflow-y-auto … h-full`) and BrowsePane.vue:4-27 places the SearchBar and its filter trigger inside the SCROLLING body, below the sticky header. With BROWSE_PAGE_SIZE = 50 (useBrowsePalettes.ts:18) plus pagination, a user must scroll the wall back to the top to re-search or re-filter. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3 law 8 (fixtures must not out-compete the protagonist) is inverted: the pinned element is the pane's caption, which additionally runs the scroll-driven shrink at PaneHeader.vue:177-194 (the MQ-1 PRM blind spot). No pass in the 12-file corpus mentions the field's scroll behaviour — `grep -rn sticky challenge-*.md` returns only L-axis rows describing PaneHeader as 'renders the Card root + sticky header'.

missed.claim: INFO — `role="list"` never contains a `listitem` in ANY state of this wall: populated it holds `role="article"` cards, empty it holds a `role="status"` plate rendered inside the list.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 sets `role="list"`; its slotted children are PaletteCard roots with `role="article"` (PaletteCard.vue:22) — pass-2 D-12 owns that half — but the empty plate at PaletteCardGrid.vue:21-31 is rendered INSIDE the same list element and resolves to EmptyState.vue:28's `role="status"` div. So in the zero-result / true-empty state a live status region is an owned child of a list, which is not a permitted list child, and the list is announced as having zero items over content that is speaking. Extends D-12 rather than duplicating it: the honest statement is that no state of this container produces a valid list.

superlatives: The colour-surface roster is genuinely excellent design-system engineering and is the reason D5-01 is a defect rather than an absence: ONE named roster, declared once with its rationale at the point of declaration (demo/styles/foundation.css:653-657, :659-663), reused VERBATIM by both @media (forced-colors: active) (:678-696) and @media print (:829-841) so the 'keep the colours' set can never drift between registers, and carrying an explicit consumer extension point ([data-color-surface]) that costs a new colour surface one attribute — and, because forced-color-adjust and print-color-adjust are both inherited, one attribute on a parent.

PaletteCardSkeleton is the rare loading primitive that announces itself and refuses to fork the producer: role="status" aria-label="Loading palette" on its own root (PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:32-37), two temporal registers split by WAIT SPECIES not by decoration (`shadow` = known-imminent local compute, `developing` = unknown-duration network), and a stagger that rides glass-ui's --skeleton-shimmer-delay / --skeleton-shimmer-tint seams and is 'never re-defined here' (:17-22). Its comment states the invariant the rest of the app should be judged by: loading ≠ empty splits on ANNOUNCEMENT, not motion.

EmptyState separates the two plate species at the ROLE level, not the styling level — role="alert" for error (EmptyState.vue:14-27) and role="status" for the invitation (:28-65) — with genuinely different registers (the error arm drops the eyebrow and the ghost trio) and a CTA slot terminated in both (:26, :64). The atom is right; only the call site under-uses it, which is exactly what makes D5-04 a one-line cure.

The pane's motion is centrally governed and it obeys the governance rather than re-implementing it: the one transition BrowsePane authors inline is `transition-opacity duration-fast` (BrowsePane.vue:88), and opacity is precisely the property BOTH PRM guards preserve (codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md §1 — guard 2 rewrites the transition property list to opacity/color/background-color/border-color/box-shadow), so the sort/search wash degrades correctly by construction and not by patch; the state morph keys the shared `vj-morph` family defined in demo/styles/animations.css rather than ad hoc in the component.

PaletteColorStrip's weighted-segment model is a real design idea, correctly implemented: per-segment proportions from the palette's own `weight` fields with an 8% legibility floor and a re-normalisation pass (PaletteColorStrip.vue:47-71), so an extracted palette carries its population story onto the card while small clusters stay visible — and the component takes its corner radius from the parent's fallthrough class rather than restating it (PaletteCard.vue:36).

The corpus's own restraint is worth recording: challenge-D-design.md §5.4 declines to born-RED an owner-ruled single-instance exception; §5.3 kills its own promising 'the strip lost its radius' hypothesis; §5.6 corrects the prior pass's reproduction premise from a measurement rather than an argument; C pass-2 N-6/N-7 retract two of pass-1's own findings; and L pass-6's N-L6 stops a plausible demo repair by proving the producer surface does not exist at 7.0.0 (searchVariants.d.ts = inline|bare|floating). Twelve passes with that much self-correction are why the few overreaches above stand out.
unproven: D5-01's print limb ('so the wall also does not print') — print-color-adjust: economy only LICENSES the engine to drop backgrounds; the axis's own evidence/D-p5-wall-print.png shows the strips painting under emulated print media. The honest form is 'the specimen prints only if the user opts into Background graphics, while the roster surfaces print unconditionally'. Deciding it needs a real print/PDF pipeline. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

P-1's Vue-internal deadlock mechanism (out-in holding isLeaving so the pending child never mounts) and its unrecoverability across search / clear / route re-entry / backend restore. Every precondition is confirmed in the live source and three seats measured the blank, but I could not re-run the probe. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE (finding CONFIRMED on preconditions + triple independent measurement; mechanism label unverified here).

P-4's production-data census ('5 of the 10 live public rows carry oklabColors: []') and P-2/P-3's live cliff table — production-API measurements, not decidable from the tree. The predicate asymmetry that makes them inevitable IS decidable and is confirmed.

All computed-style and pixel figures carried by the governing D file (D5-03's Δluminance 0.0 vs 96.8, D5-05's 20.352/18.608/16.4/11px, D5-02's statusRegions: 1, D5-01's stripDistinctBg) were measured by those seats; I verified only their structural preconditions, which hold in every case I could reach statically.

The forced-colors frame was captured under Playwright's forcedColors: "active" EMULATION, not a real OS high-contrast theme (the aurora ground still paints in the frame). The roster omission that causes it is proven statically and is theme-independent, but the exact substituted colours a real WHCM user sees are not.

My missed finding M4 (sticky header vs scrolling search) is proven structurally; the size of the user cost — how far a reader of a 50-card wall must scroll back — is a live-measurement question I did not run.

result.verdict: SOURCE-RED AFFIRMED AND WIDENED — the corpus was right about the catalog and the ink, wrong about its own blast radii, and blind to its two worst crashes (the two-click powerless-hue pane kill and the 28-grey boot white-screen, both measured against the shipped dist and re-reproduced byte-identically on resume). Dispositions ADJUDICATED, not VERIFIED.

confirmed.claim: `loadingMore` is stranded TRUE for the session; the load-more affordance dies permanently after any concurrent reload.
confirmed.proof: LIVE SOURCE `demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:112` — `finally { if (gen === loadGeneration) loadingMore.value = false; }`. I enumerated every writer of the flag: `grep -rn loadingMore demo/` returns exactly 5 non-doc sites — declaration `:29`, the guard `:98`, the set-true `:101`, the generation-gated set-false `:112`, and the port re-export `usePalettePorts.ts:162`. (5) `:6657-6666` — `remove()` for a Fragment with `patchFlag & 2048` iterates children and calls `remove(child)`; the child's `transition` is the stale enter-hooks object, whose `afterLeave` is `undefined`, so `:6677-6680` `performRemove` removes the element and calls nothing. (6) `:1382-1384` — every subsequent render returns `emptyPlaceholder(child)` while `state.isLeaving`, which is what the pass-3 probe photographed as `"elementChildren": 0` with `<!---->` in the grid. For a single-root component step (2) reaches the element and the resume fires — which is why the `developing → error` transition works and only `error → *` strands. `PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11` documents this precise hazard in its own source ("a leading comment node would make this a multi-root component"), so the convention exists in this repo and `EmptyState.vue` violates it.

missed.claim: CLASS-LEVEL, and it undermines the evidence base of this whole audit programme: 31 demo SFCs place a comment before the root element, so they render as multi-root fragments in dev and single-root elements in production. Dev and prod therefore execute DIFFERENT Vue code paths for these components — `getChildRoot`/attribute fallthrough, transition-hook propagation, and `$el` resolution are all `__DEV__`-gated. Every probe in this corpus ran against the dev server.
missed.proof: Scanning every `demo/**/*.vue` for a comment as the first template child returns 31 files, including `demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue`, `demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue`, `PaletteCardMeta.vue`, `ActionFeedback.vue`, `PaletteColorStrip.vue`, `PaletteCardSkeleton.vue`, `ShadowPalette.vue`, `browser/status/ApiOfflineChip.vue`, `demo/shared/ui/PaneHeader.vue` — i.e. most of the Browse wall. The dev/prod split is decidable and I decided it: `@vue/compiler-core/dist/compiler-core.cjs.js:2308` has `comments: true`; `compiler-core.cjs.prod.js:2304` has `comments: false`; `compiler-core/index.js` switches on `process.env.NODE_ENV`; the prod dist emits no `2048` patchflag at all. I compiled `EmptyState.vue` under all four (NODE_ENV × isProd) combinations — NODE_ENV alone decides (`isProd` is inert for this). `vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:34456` sets `process.env.NODE_ENV = defaultNodeEnv` before `loadConfigFromFile`, and `@vitejs/plugin-vue/dist/index.mjs` resolves the compiler lazily, so `vite build` compiles with the prod compiler. In the runtime, `runtime-core.cjs.js:4578-4580` (`getChildRoot`) and `:6659` (the fragment-transition branch) are both `__DEV__`-only in Vue's source. Consequence: for those 31 components, a dev-server observation about fallthrough class/attr application, transition behaviour, or `$el` does not transfer to production, and vice versa — which is exactly how P-1 came to be reported as a production BLOCKER.

superlatives: EXCELLENT — the self-alias generation at `vite.config.ts:37-50`. The demo's alias set for `@mkbabb/value.js/*` is *generated* from `package.json#exports` with anchored regexes, so an alias cannot drift from the export map nor prefix-match into a subpath. I re-derived the negative independently: `BrowsePane.vue`'s fourteen imports (`:179-199`) are `vue`, demo-relative paths and one published subpath; `package.json#exports` has exactly seven keys and `src/subpaths/color.ts` publishes no distance metric, so an unauthorable specifier really is unauthorable. Three separate seats reached this same conclusion by three methods. This is the single best-engineered structural guarantee in the component's blast radius and must survive any restructure verbatim.

EXCELLENT — `demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11`. The file puts its explanatory comment *inside* the root `<div>` and says why in the source: "a leading comment node would make this a multi-root component, and PalettesPane reads `$el` for useSortable — a fragment root resolves $el to the comment node, not the <div>." The consumer it protects is real (`PalettesPane.vue:181` reads `(sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el`). A subtle Vue-internals hazard, understood, documented at the site, and correctly avoided — which is precisely why `EmptyState.vue`'s violation of the same rule is a regression against a known standard rather than an unknowable.

EXCELLENT — `useBrowsePalettes.ts:200-207`, the `onSetVisibility` guarded patch. Under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` it builds `const patch: Partial<Palette> = { updatedAt }` and conditionally adds `visibility`/`published`/`currentHash` only when the response actually resolved them, with the reason stated in the comment. That is the rare case of a strict-TS constraint being honoured by construction instead of cast away — in the same file that elsewhere flattens a whole typed error hierarchy to a string literal.

EXCELLENT — the named-re-export discipline across the six cluster barrels (`browser/card/index.ts:1-3`, `browser/search/index.ts:1-2`, `browser/dialog/index.ts:1-5`). Never a star re-export, with the tree-shake rationale spelled out (an SFC's scoped `<style>` is a side-effecting import). This is the reason L6-2's admin-component leak costs zero shipped bytes, and the reason pass 3's Probe B measured byte-identical output when it forced `moduleSideEffects: true`.

EXCELLENT — the audit provenance discipline itself. Six L-seats and three C-seats each archived their predecessor byte-identically with an `md5 -q` receipt (`challenge-L-library.md:30-34`), ran a measured novelty scan before claiming novelty (`:57-69`), deferred to the stronger prior proof in an explicit table rather than re-litigating, and retracted their own findings in writing when a predecessor had proved the sharper claim (`challenge-L-library.md:304-319`; `challenge-C-implementation.md:374-395` withdrawing pass 2's `[30,30]` double-mount multiplier while preserving the leak). Pass 5's negative control on the ref-identity probe (`control_remotePalettes_vs_savedPalettes: false`) and pass 5-D's own stub-bug confession (`votes` vs `voteCount`) are the same instinct. That is the hygiene that let me find N-6's cure and P-1's real mechanism instead of re-deriving the corpus.
